# Frederik Frede

> Brand strategy, identity and digital for design-led culture. Independent creative director and brand strategist, Berlin and Los Angeles.

Frederik Frede is an independent creative director and brand strategist working across culture, strategy and identity, based in Berlin and Los Angeles. Thirty years across brand strategy, visual identity, editorial and digital; co-founder of Freunde von Freunden and MoreSleep. Building brands, platforms and experiences for people who care how things look and last, each held to the same question: does it earn its place, or just add to the noise.

The work organizes around three groups: culture (the world the practice reads), strategy (how the practice thinks), identity (how the practice makes). Every project is filtered through timelessness, authenticity and usability.

This file holds the text of every page on frederikfrede.com. A shorter index is at https://frederikfrede.com/llms.txt.

---

## Information. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/about.html

Creative Director with 30+ years experience in brand strategy, identity and digital. Co-founder of MoreSleep and Freunde von Freunden. Now working independently, globally.

Built on design and creativity, scaled through agency life, platform building and studio founding. From selling NoMoreSleep to TBWA, to growing Freunde von Freunden into one of Europe's most referenced creative platforms, to running an internationally dispersed studio across Berlin and Los Angeles. The through line was never a category or a sector. It was a way of seeing.

Working closely with founders, clients and collaborators who share that ambition. Across strategy, identity, and the thinking that connects them.

#### Services

Strategy

Brand positioning, research, naming, and messaging. The thinking that gives design a reason to exist.

Identity

Visual identity systems, typography, art direction, and print. Built for longevity, not trend cycles.

Digital

Website design, platform strategy, social systems, and campaign architecture. Coherent across every touchpoint.

Editorial

Content strategy, publishing, and campaign direction. From single stories to book-length projects.

Production

Film, photography, motion, and events. Creative leadership from concept through delivery.

AI & Consulting

Frameworks and workflows that make creative work faster, sharper, and more considered.

#### Approach

Some people arrive at design through a career. For me it was always present. A quiet obsession with why some details feel right and others just exist.

That feeling never left. It just found bigger rooms to work in.

Everything gets filtered through the same three lenses: timelessness, authenticity, and usability. Not as a methodology. As a way of seeing. What earns its place in someone's life and what is just decoration without relevance. What lasts and what was only ever noise.

It shows up in the work. And everywhere else.

## AI & Brand Consulting. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/ai-consulting.html

Brand strategy and identity built with AI as a thinking partner. Consulting for companies working out what AI means for their brand, their content and their teams.

Every engagement now runs with AI as a working partner. Not a production shortcut. A thinking tool, present from the first brief.

Umane shows the method. Strategy, naming, identity and a full design system, developed in conversation with Claude and pressure-tested against the brand's own logic in real time. Delivered in two layers: guidelines for people, a structured system of YAML and Markdown for agents. Same brand, two formats.

The setup has a name: Directive Intelligence. A digital mind. Thirty years of standards, references and voice, written down so a machine can follow them. It drafts, compares and argues the way the practice does.

Tools are chosen per task, never the other way around. Claude and GPT in combination, each where it is strongest. Figma carries the design work. Higgsfield, Reve and After Effects carry image and motion. The framework decides what runs where.

The consulting side works the other way around. Companies bring questions about what AI means for their brand, their content and their teams. The answers arrive as working prototypes, not slide decks.

In the field

Umane, built with Claude from the first brief Architonic, Smart Search Directive Intelligence, in the wild

Selected engagements

- NZZ Mediengruppe 2025-2026

- Umane 2025-2026

- SamSation 2025-2026

- Architonic 2024-2025

- Swayed 2018

Working out what AI means for a brand starts with a conversation. Get in touch.

## Hospitality Branding. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/hospitality.html

Brand strategy, identity and digital for hotels, restaurants, clubs and hospitality groups. Nineteen projects across Europe, the Americas and Georgia.

Hotels, restaurants, members' clubs, a coffee space in the LA Arts District. Nineteen hospitality brands over two decades, from a Roaring Twenties gala at the Ritz-Carlton Berlin to the identity that helped put Georgian hotels on the map.

Hospitality brands live or die on atmosphere. The work starts there. What a place feels like at its best, then a system that carries that feeling across every surface: the room, the menu, the website, the booking confirmation.

In the field

## Real Estate Branding. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/real-estate.html

Brand strategy, identity and digital for property developers and real estate brands. From a family-owned California developer to towers in Buenos Aires and lofts in Kreuzberg.

Real estate is the most emotional and most expensive thing most people ever buy. The brand work has to carry that weight. Eight developer and property brands, from a family-owned California firm with sixty years of history to a residential tower in Buenos Aires.

The method is the same each time. Find what the place actually stands for, then build the system that sells it: identity, sales collateral, photography direction, and a digital presence that shows the property the way a visit would.

In the field

Lewis Group of Companies Engel & Völkers Berlin Ziegert, Kreuzberg lofts

## 25hours Hotels. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/25hours-hotels-brand-identity.html

Editorial design, digital strategy and video production for 25hours Hotels, including Companion magazine and the opening film for the 25hours Hotel Bikini Berlin.

Hotels

Editorial · Digital · Film

"A page-turning magazine, and a moving portrait of every hotel."

Editorial design and digital strategy for Companion, the in-house magazine of 25hours Hotels, alongside video and content production across the group, including the opening of the 25hours Hotel Bikini Berlin.

German boutique chain 25hours Hotels launched in 2005 and now have 13 hotels in nine cities including Vienna, Hamburg and Paris. Known for their daring, whimsy and attention to detail, each property has its own individual story.

We paired with 25hours to create a unique print magazine called Companion, a joint project with our editorial arm Friends of Friends, tapping into our global network of trusted creatives from art, design, architecture, music, gastronomy, sport and beyond.

01 — Publication Design

#### A full-colour tabloid for curious travellers.

Companion is designed like a classic tabloid newspaper: a front page draws in readers with eye-catching photos, fonts and headlines of different sizes, inviting them to turn the page. City guides and full-length interviews mingle with cultural tips and playlists, in English and German.

02 — Digital

#### From print to pixels.

Companion's concept, design and development is done entirely by us. 25hours liked it so much that our Companion pieces now scroll across the front of their website as well, offering a window into the 25hours culture worldwide.

03 — Film & Content Production

#### Bringing every hotel to the screen.

Beyond Companion, we ran video and content production across the group, including the opening party for the 25hours Hotel Bikini Berlin. For each property we wrote and produced scripted introduction films, now running on screens in every hotel and online, giving every city its own moving portrait.

Full film ↗

Full film ↗

Full film ↗

Full film ↗

Full film ↗

Full film ↗

Every city has a story. We help 25hours tell it.

25hours Hotels is one of Europe's most distinctive boutique hotel groups: each property has its own personality, neighbourhood, and cultural programme. Their in-house magazine, Companion, needed to reflect this individuality, on the page and on screen.

We designed Companion as a proper publication: editorial in structure, rich in photography, and designed to be kept rather than discarded. Alongside it, we produced video content for the group, from the opening party at the 25hours Hotel Bikini Berlin to scripted films introducing each hotel, now playing on screens across all locations.

Live site: www.25hours-hotels.com ↗

Collaborators: Friends of Friends

Year: 2017

## Ace & Tate. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/ace-tate-heimatbound-campaign.html

An editorial portrait series for Ace & Tate, exploring why young creatives chose Berlin as the place to build their careers.

Tate

Campaign · Editorial · Event

Heimatbound: portraits of a city chosen as home.

An editorial portrait series for Ace & Tate, exploring why young creatives chose Berlin as the place to build their careers.

A joint series with Ace & Tate produced portraits of young, talented creatives who followed Berlin's pull as a creative haven, centred on the conflicting nature of relocation and what the city holds for each of them.

Four portraits featured musician Mikey Woodbridge, illustrator Ruohan Wang, Berlin Feminist Film Week founder Karin Fornander and DJ Nico Adomako, each photographed in their own choice of Ace & Tate frames.

01 — A Collaborative Collection

#### From portrait to product.

Each subject's choice of frames became a collaborative collection featured on Ace & Tate's online store. Services spanned talent research, content concept, creative direction, four editorial interview productions, guest management, event production, printed collateral and photography documentation.

02 — Four Portraits

#### Four moves to Berlin.

Each portrait follows one move to the city and what it changed. The interviews ran on Friends of Friends in December 2018.

## AD Magazin. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/ad-magazin-web-design-art-direction.html

Website redesign for Architectural Digest Germany: a modular, device-adaptive design that lets the content reign and gives AD's beautiful editorials room to breathe.

Magazin

Digital

"An online magazine as elegant as its readers."

Website redesign for Architectural Digest Germany: a modular, device-adaptive design that lets the content reign and gives AD's beautiful editorials room to breathe.

Architectural Digest Germany is a digital and print publication covering the best style, architecture, interiors and design from Deutschland and beyond. A website redesign that is easy to navigate and lets the content lead.

A modular system gives AD's editorials and images room on any device. A variety of options and sizes for images and text give the online platform the feel of a real magazine, with an elegant header and fonts that tie everything together.

01 — Web Design

#### Editorial feel at every scroll depth.

A sophisticated new design reveals the bounty of AD Magazin's content on the front page. Effortless scrolling and subtle navigation through features, design tips and product pages keeps readers engaged for longer.

02 — AD Design Award · 2016

#### An award night in the Friends Space.

Each year AD Germany honours young designers whose objects stand out with the AD Design Award. Friends of Friends hosted the 2016 ceremony and dinner in the Friends Space in Kreuzberg.

A digital publication as refined as the homes it covers.

Architectural Digest Germany is a digital and print publication covering the best in style, architecture, interiors, and design. A website redesign that is easy to navigate and lets the content lead.

The modular design works on any device. A range of image and text formats gives the platform the feel of a printed magazine. An elegant header and refined typography tie it together. Effortless scrolling and subtle navigation through features, design tips, and product pages keeps readers engaged longer.

Live site: www.ad-magazin.de ↗

Year: 2018

## adidas Journeys. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/adidas-journeys-interactive-campaign.html

An immersive digital storytelling campaign for adidas, going beyond product to explore the personal stories and journeys of athletes and creatives connected to the brand.

Journeys

Campaign · Digital · Content

"An interactive journey shows another side of adidas."

An immersive digital storytelling campaign for adidas, going beyond product to explore the personal stories and journeys of athletes and creatives connected to the brand.

Strategy, concept and design for adidas that put storytelling first, with bespoke online and offline experiences under the Journeys banner.

The interactive Journeys experience allowed bike enthusiasts to embark on a breathtaking tour of Italy's Südtirol through the eyes of eight different cyclists from around Europe. The website showcases detailed information on each rider and each leg of the route, with glorious photos of all the peaks and valleys.

01 — Digital Experience

#### Storytelling as the product.

A rich interactive platform that documents the riders, the route, and the race in real time, blending editorial depth with an intuitive digital journey.

02 — Editorial & Content

#### Portraits, diaries, and lookbooks.

With Friends of Friends, editorial video portraits of selected adidas riders and the people they met along the route, plus personal photos and reflections collected into an online diary and lookbook. The films were made in partnership with Südtirol.

One portrait follows Berlin photographer and Journeys team member David Fischer, who got his start shooting friends at bike races.

David Fischer Photographer and team rider · full portrait

Claudio Camin Camin Bikes · Bolzano

Claudio Camin Second cut · Bolzano

Norbert Niederkofler St. Hubertus · Alta Badia

Sport as a story worth following.

The brief from adidas went beyond the product campaign: a digital experience that told the personal stories behind the brand's global community of athletes, creatives, and culture-shapers.

Adidas Journeys was an interactive storytelling platform: long-form editorial, documentary photography, and an interface designed to draw people deeper into each story. A different adidas to the one you see in broadcast.

Live site: www.adidas.com ↗

Collaborators: Friends of Friends

Year: 2013

## Adobe. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/adobe-creative-cloud-stock-films.html

Films for Adobe Creative Cloud and Adobe Stock, produced with Friends of Friends in Barcelona, Vienna, Berlin and London between 2017 and 2018.

Editorial · Film

"The people behind the work."

Films for Adobe Creative Cloud and Adobe Stock, produced with Friends of Friends in Barcelona, Vienna, Berlin and London between 2017 and 2018.

Adobe worked with Friends of Friends on a run of productions for Creative Cloud and Adobe Stock. The approach came from the FvF magazine. Real creatives, filmed in their own studios and cities. The software shows up where it belongs, inside the work.

A workshop film from TYPO Berlin came first. A tutorial series, an event film in Berlin and a photographer portrait in London followed.

01 — Modular Lettering

#### Two studios, one alphabet.

Illustrators Birgit Palma and Daniel Triendl ran Adobe's Modular Lettering workshops in 2017. Participants built letters from a shared set of geometric modules and worked on the same file at the same time through Creative Cloud.

The film starts in their studios in Barcelona and Vienna. It ends at TYPO Berlin, where the two led the workshop at Haus der Kulturen der Welt. Released on Adobe Germany's YouTube channel in July 2017.

On the FvF site the film ran with an essay on collaboration in the cloud and how shared files change the way design gets made.

02 — Tutorials and events

#### From workshop to series.

The lettering film set the tone for a tutorial series on InDesign and Photoshop. Two designers, three videos each. Every episode shows a designer's own relationship with the tool, then how to use it.

A two-day Adobe Stock contributor event took place at the FvF Friends Space in Berlin. The post-event film follows the contributor workshop, with short statements from guests on camera.

03 — Contributor Spotlight

#### A city of many origins.

Contributor Spotlight introduces the photographers behind the Adobe Stock collection. This film follows London photographer and Adobe Stock Premium contributor Andy Smith.

Adobe had commissioned him to shoot London for its Multilocalism visual trend. Real people instead of models. A cab driver, a barber, a butcher, a crossing guard, each photographed at work. The film stays close to his way of working. People first, then location, then the story that grows between them.

For me the interest in photography was always about people.

Productions for Adobe Germany and Adobe Creative Cloud, 2017 to 2018, made through FvF Productions. Each one came out of the same network. Designers and photographers, filmed in the places where they work.

Andy Smith's London series can be seen on the Adobe blog.

## Architonic. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/architonic-brand-strategy-platform-design.html

Full rebrand, platform redesign, and campaign for Architonic: Europe's leading platform for architectural products.

tonic

Strategy · Identity · Digital · Campaign · AI · Consulting

"Ideas. Specified."

A complete rebrand, platform redesign, and global campaign for Europe's leading architectural products platform, evolving Architonic from database to living workspace.

Architonic helped architects reach products and materials back when brand sites were bad and access was gated. That problem solved itself. Better tooling, open catalogues, and now AI closing the gap fast. The platform was still answering a question nobody was asking. Audience was drifting. The model underneath it was starting to show.

The work was not a redesign. It was getting the eye back on the prize, before the lead disappeared. New brand strategy, new identity, a full platform redesign, and a campaign to launch it. The shift was the whole point: from product database to living workspace. From first sketch to final spec. In one place. Ideas. Specified.

OOH — Milan Campaign launch during Salone del Mobile. Duomo metro station takeover, May 2025.

01 — Identity

#### A mark built for confidence at every scale.

The new identity centres on a bolder, more confident wordmark: stacked, compressed, unmissable. Coral red was already in Architonic's DNA; we made it the undisputed brand colour across every surface. The underscore beneath the wordmark became a structural signature: a platform, a foundation, a line to build from. The system had to work in a phone notification and on the wall of a Milanese apartment building. It does both.

From database to living workspace. Ideas. Specified.

02 — Platform Design

#### Search rebuilt for the way architects actually think.

The product redesign started from how architects and designers actually research: by image, by material, by a half-formed idea. Smart Search with natural language. Visual Search that accepts a photo and returns the closest match. A 3D configurator for real-time material exploration. Live Link keeps every spec sheet current the moment a manufacturer updates it.

The same problem got answered at the product level too. If the old reason to exist was easy access, the new one had to be where people actually work. AT Studio is that move: collaborative boards that replace the email chain with one interactive canvas, where discovery, specification, and the back-and-forth all happen in the same place. Built so the platform is where the work lives, not just where it gets found.

03 — Campaign

#### The ultimate tool for research and collaboration.

The relaunch campaign distilled the new Architonic into a single promise: a living workspace that carries an idea from the line to a fully reliable specification. Bold kinetic poster design, layered typography, and the coral palette, designed to stop you in a Milan metro corridor at 8am. The campaign ran across the Milan metro network during Salone del Mobile, digital, and trade press, reaching architects at the exact moment they were most immersed in product discovery.

Campaign "The ultimate tool for research and collaboration", the final campaign poster, designed for large-format street display.

03 — Campaign · Studios

#### Studios speak.

The campaign proof layer launched alongside the posters and film: real architects and designers using Architonic in their actual workflow. Four pillars, four studios. Discover. Design. Trust. Deliver.

Kinzo Berlin Design Together

OOS Zurich Discover Smarter · Trust the Data

Ippolito Fleitz Group Stuttgart

Sigurd Larsen Berlin

04 — Film

#### The relaunch film.

A 90-second platform film launched June 12, 2025: site takeover, social activation, and trade press simultaneously. Five narrative chapters: Spark, Shape, Trust, Momentum, Invitation. The coral branding, four-word supers, and logo animations act as visual glue throughout.

Film Architonic relaunch summary film with subtitles. Launch: architonic.com, June 12 2025.

Motion AT brand loop: the identity in motion, used across digital channels and social.

Europe's leading platform for architectural products and materials, trusted for over two decades. The original edge was access, back when brand sites were bad and catalogues were gated. That edge was gone, and the model built on it was starting to show.

The rebrand ran across every layer of the business: brand strategy and positioning, visual identity, a full platform redesign, and a global launch campaign. The shift was the point. From product database to living workspace. One environment where discovery, collaboration, and specification happen in the same place, AT Studio included.

The campaign launched at Salone del Mobile 2025. A Milan metro takeover at Duomo station, a 90-second hero film, a testimonial series with leading studios, and a full digital activation. It reached architects at the moment they were deepest in product research.

Live site: architonic.com ↗

Year: 2023–2025

## Bianca Chen. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/bianca-chen-brand-identity.html

Brand strategy, visual identity and web design for Bianca Chen, independent curator based in Los Angeles.

Chen

Strategy · Identity · Digital · Motion

"Curated Chaos"

A full brand strategy, visual identity, and digital presence for an independent Los Angeles curator, daughter of legendary tastemaker JF Chen.

Bianca Chen is a curator in Los Angeles and the daughter of JF Chen, one of the most respected names in the field. That is a starting point and a weight at the same time. Going independent meant building a brand that stood on its own without cutting the lineage loose, recognisable as hers, not a continuation of the family name.

The work started before any mark was drawn. Strategy first: purpose, audience, positioning. The identity, Curated Chaos, holds traditional and contemporary work in the same frame and gives her a presence that reads as her own. Heritage in the room, not running the room.

01 — Brand Strategy & Identity

#### Curated Chaos as a design language.

The visual identity runs on a vibrant palette that reflects the energy and diversity of Los Angeles while embodying Bianca's curatorial style and heritage. It pairs the typefaces New Edge 666 by Charlotte Rohde and Bookish by Helsinki Type, a functional but distinctive typographic and layout approach that carries "Curated Chaos" across every touchpoint.

02 — Print & Collateral

#### An identity that travels off-screen.

The brand system extends across posters, business cards, tote bags and wristbands, all carrying the same energy of Curated Chaos into physical exhibition spaces and events.

03 — Digital

#### A website that curates as it showcases.

Designed and developed in Webflow, the site was built specifically to showcase Bianca's curatorial projects and capture her "Curated Chaos" style. Interactive elements including hover animations, shape-driven micro-interactions and smooth transitions contribute to a dynamic and engaging user experience.

"Curated Chaos": tradition and disruption in one identity.

Bianca Chen is an independent curator based in Los Angeles, devoted to elevating the city's diverse art landscape and championing emerging artists from around the world.

The brand strategy was built from scratch: purpose, audiences, positioning, and narrative defined before a single mark was drawn. The identity, Curated Chaos, captures Los Angeles's energy through a vibrant palette and a functional but distinctive typographic and layout approach.

The Webflow website showcases Bianca's curatorial projects, with hover animations and interactive elements that carry her approach through. It works as a hub for exploring her exhibitions, upcoming projects, and philanthropic initiatives supporting economic opportunity and gender equity for artisans worldwide.

Live site: biancachen.com ↗

Elegant yet casual, market-fresh and shared.

The rich teal branding colour echoes the earthy colours of produce while balancing well with interior elements such as green tiles and indoor plants.

Brutø's identity brings to life its focus on elegant yet casual dining and a modern menu of seasonal, shared plates — including a custom order sheet that guests fill out themselves at the table.

## CLOSED. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/closed-editorial-portrait-series.html

2015–2022 partnership with fashion brand CLOSED: a portrait series in seven cities, campaign films, press days and a 40th-anniversary dinner.

Campaign · Editorial · Content · Event

Portraits, films and long tables for a denim label.

2015–2022 partnership with fashion brand CLOSED: an ongoing portrait series in seven cities, campaign films, two seasons of press days and a 40th-anniversary dinner, produced by Friends of Friends and FvF Productions.

CLOSED has made clothes since 1978. The label started in Italy, moved its headquarters to Hamburg in 1990 and still has its jeans made in Italy. It stands for denim and pieces built to be worn for years. The partnership showed that attitude through people: the team behind the label, and creatives who wear it in their daily lives.

Friends of Friends and FvF Productions worked with CLOSED from 2015 to 2022. It began with two seasons of press days at the FvF Apartment and a film series for the Archive ’85 campaign. In 2018 the label celebrated 40 years with a dinner at the Friends Space, and an editorial portrait series began. It visited a painter in Antwerp, a photographer in the Uckermark and creatives in New York, Berlin, Los Angeles, Milan and Amsterdam. A new round of portraits followed in 2022. The stories ran on Friends of Friends and across CLOSED’s website, online shop, social channels and print magazine HARD COPY.

##### Formats and years

2015

German Press Days

Two seasons of collection presentations at the FvF Apartment, Berlin

2015

Archive ’85

A brand film, four team portraits and an interview for the AW15/16 campaign

2018

40 years of CLOSED

An Italian dinner for 120 guests at the Friends Space, Berlin, and a dinner with talk in November

2018–2019

Portrait series

Creatives in Antwerp, the Uckermark, New York, Berlin, Los Angeles, Milan and Amsterdam

2020

A Better Blue

A story on the label’s reduced-impact denim

2022

Tastemakers

Three portraits in Los Angeles and Berlin

01 — German Press Days · 2015

#### A collection, at home in an apartment.

Twice a year, German Press Days bring fashion press to Berlin. For two seasons in 2015, CLOSED moved its press showroom into the FvF Apartment, the furnished flat Friends of Friends used for events, workshops and guests. Rails, mannequins and a long dining table took the place of a trade-fair booth. The AW15 collection hung in rooms that felt lived in.

##### CLOSED at the FvF Apartment

See the project on Friends of Friends ↗

02 — Archive ’85 · 2015

#### The people behind the label.

For autumn/winter 2015, CLOSED looked back at its own history. The Archive ’85 collection brought back denim styles from the 1980s. Friends of Friends built the campaign content around the people who make the company. A brand film and four short portraits introduce the team, with sales staff in New York, Paris, Amsterdam and Copenhagen. A long interview with co-owner Til Nadler, at home and at the Hamburg headquarters, ran on Friends of Friends.

03 — 40 years of CLOSED · 2018

#### Forty years, one long Italian dinner.

CLOSED jeans have been made in Italy for four decades, from the first weave to the final wash. To mark 40 years, the label hosted an Italian concept dinner at the Friends Space in Kreuzberg. 120 guests sat at long tables under gold pendant lamps. Friends of the brand at the table included Rabea Schif, Jochen Schropp, Caro Daur and Sara Nuru.

A second evening followed on 21 November 2018. A talk on the sofa first, then dinner at long candlelit tables.

04 — Portrait series · 2018–2019

#### Creative practice, close to home.

The portrait series started in 2018 as Men in Closed and grew into an ongoing editorial format. Each episode places the season’s collection in the daily life, studio and neighbourhood of a creative. Friends of Friends handled concept, research and casting, the visual narrative, photography and text. Together with FvF Productions, the team developed a storytelling style and a visual identity that fit the CLOSED aesthetic.

Every portrait was adapted for CLOSED’s international website, online shop, social channels and the print magazine HARD COPY, and ran in full on Friends of Friends. In autumn 2019 the productions continued with art director Zipeng Zhu in New York and Gunifort Uwambaga of the Amsterdam bookshop and publisher MENDO.

05 — A Better Blue · 2020

#### Denim with a smaller footprint.

In 2020 a Friends of Friends story looked at the sustainability programme behind CLOSED denim. A Better Blue is a reduced-impact line made with the Italian mill Candiani, which supplies most of the label’s denim. It began with two fabrics and grew to two thirds of the denim range. Denim developer Uwe Kippschnieder and head of production Nina Schlüter explained how it is made.

##### A cleaner thread

Read the story on Friends of Friends ↗

06 — Tastemakers · 2022

#### From Los Angeles to Berlin.

It visited creative director Nu Goteh, co-founder of Room for Magic and its publication Deem, at his Spanish-style 1920s home in South Los Angeles. ## Concierge Coffee. Brand & Web. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/concierge-coffee-brand-web.html

Brand strategy, identity direction, and headless e-commerce for Concierge Coffee, a material-driven coffee space in the LA Arts District, rooted between Berlin and Los Angeles.

Coffee

Strategy · Identity · E-Commerce

"Coffee as a cultural vehicle, not the hero."

A coffee roaster with a room in the LA Arts District and a bar in Berlin. Brand strategy, identity direction, and a store that lives inside the site rather than beside it. Live at conciergecoffee.com since 29 September 2026.

Concierge Coffee sits at 821 Traction Avenue, sharing an entrance with Departamento. Founded by Benjamin and Namy. The interior by Klein Agency is raw, material, unhurried. The coffee is the constant.

The brief, in the founders' words: a people-oriented space for straight-forward specialty coffee. Elevated simplicity. Exceptional service. The work covered positioning, identity direction and a full e-commerce site for two cities at once, Los Angeles first.

01 — Brand Strategy

#### Between two cities. Neither explaining itself.

Berlin brings underground credibility and neighbourhood permanence. Los Angeles brings lifestyle energy and collab culture. The brand does not try to bridge the two. It lives in both.

#### Coffee as a cultural vehicle, not the hero.

Warm, confident, lightly playful, and never precious about it. No artisanal, no third wave, none of the language every roaster reaches for. Mood over product, hands and textures over hero shots. Coffee as the vehicle, culture as the cargo.

A material-driven space to slow down.

02 — Identity

#### The mark already existed.

Crossed keys and a serif wordmark, drawn in 2014. For months the site ran on a placeholder because nobody had the vector. The fix was a request for the original Illustrator file, not a trace of the packshot. The mark now sits in the nav and the footer as one inline drawing, inverting on dark sections without a second asset.

#### Newsreader, Helvetica Neue, black and white.

Headlines in Newsreader, the same Scotch roman lineage as the wordmark, redrawn for screens. Everything else in Helvetica Neue. No decoration. Packaging in two colourways, Aesop-like in its restraint. Dark green for espresso, khaki for filter. Kraft bag, printed front, roast date by hand.

03 — The Space

#### Designed by Klein Agency. 821 Traction Ave.

Klein Agency, the Downtown LA studio of Maša and Jon Kleinhample, designed and fabricated the interior. Terrazzo bar, raw wood beam, whitewashed brick, tree-stump stools. The kind of room that makes people slow down without being told to. Their photography carries the site.

04 — The Website

#### Headless Shopify. The store inside the site.

Plain HTML, one stylesheet, two small modules. No framework, no build step. Shopify's Storefront API handles catalogue, cart and checkout in the background, so buying happens on conciergecoffee.com and only the payment page belongs to Shopify. Full-bleed photography, sparse copy, a bag drawer that reads like the rest of the page.

#### Three directions. One held.

Dark and edgy, then warm minimal, then black and white with nothing added. The last one held. Every card, panel and button was measured at 320, 390, 768 and 1440 wide before it shipped. Part of what read as restraint was text too faint to read on a bright street. One grey token, darkened to pass contrast, fixed it in fifteen places. Hosting on Cloudflare Pages under the founders' own account. Behind a password on 22 September, public on the 29th. conciergecoffee.de points to the same site.

05 — Pick-up

#### Ordered on the site, paid on Square, collected at the bar.

The bar runs on Square. Rather than a second ordering app, the site talks to Square directly. The menu comes from the till with live prices, a small bag builds on the page, and Square's hosted checkout takes the payment. The order lands on the bar's screen like any other pick-up. No card detail passes through the site.

#### The till chose the menu.

Ninety days of orders, twelve thousand of them, ranked the drinks. Iced drinks were half of everything sold. The menu opens with the four photographed drinks and runs the rest as one long list. Built, tested and wired to the till. Switched on once the bar is ready for it.

06 — Method

#### Checked at the network, not by eye.

One shared stylesheet and one shared layout, so a change lands everywhere or nowhere. A handover document in the repository records every decision with its date, its reason and what it replaced. The cart request body, the checkout URL followed to the end, the deployment checked from outside after every push.

The first drink sold through the site was a five-dollar test, refunded at the till. The first bag shipped on a test code to the founder's own address. Both before anyone else could.

Live at conciergecoffee.com, shipping across the US from Los Angeles. Four coffees, two sizes. Pick-up ordering built and waiting on the bar. The founders own the account for every service the site runs on.

Space design and photography by Klein Agency.

Live site: conciergecoffee.com ↗

Collaborators: Klein Agency (space design and photography)

Year: 2025–2026

## Directive Intelligence. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/directive-intelligence.html

Directive Intelligence: a company's voice, rules, facts and decisions in one system that people and AI tools work from. A case study.

Case study · Brand, strategy and technology for companies

Intelligence

A company's voice, rules, facts and decisions in one system. Every person and every tool works from it, and it grows with every input.

A brand lives in many hands: marketing, sales, agencies, and now their tools. Each works from its own copy, an old deck, a PDF, a quick prompt. Nobody gets it wrong on purpose. There is simply no single version.

Reality check

#### A partner poster by tomorrow. Which logo, which colour, which line?

The brand PDF

##### Somewhere in a PDF or a deck.

Page 40 of the brand PDF, or an old deck. The one designer who knows is away. The poster goes out with a guess.

The brand system

##### An answer in Slack, in seconds.

The brand system replies with the rule, the reason and the right file, then checks the draft.

Why

#### Run the company on what it already knows.

##### One center

Every business, office, agency and tool works from the same rules.

##### Faster

First drafts in minutes and in the company's voice, automatically checked before review.

##### Lower cost

Less agency time, fewer rounds, fewer errors in market.

"It is already improving our margins."Benjamin, Concierge Coffee

How it works

#### A gentle system in the background. The method sets the rhythm, people make the calls.

##### Written down

The brand and its rules in plain files, each with its reason and date.

##### Where the team already works

Slack, Figma, cloud tools or a private workspace.

##### Checked

New drafts and live pages are read against the rules before anything goes out.

##### Written back

Decisions go back in the same day. The AI suggests, people decide.

Strategy and planning

#### The thinking comes first.

##### Positioning

Where the company stands and what sets it apart, with the reasons.

##### Plans

Launches, campaigns and the year ahead, drafted from current figures.

##### The other side

The strongest case against a recommendation, before it reaches the board.

#### The technology is the same for everyone.

The difference is how it is connected and applied.

Reference · A family-owned community developer

#### One brand for five businesses across the American West, on the company's own servers.

Before

##### Many versions

A brand book, voice guide and templates in PDFs. Five ways of telling the company's age, nine taglines across four sites.

The system

##### One source

The brand rules in the company's own words, on its own servers, read by every team, agency and AI tool.

Now

##### One version

Drafts in minutes, every page checked before launch, one brand lead for five businesses.

Reference · An international publishing and media house

#### Almost 250 years of journalism, held in one system for every editor, designer and tool.

Before

##### A long memory, spread out

An archive of almost 250 years, several titles, separate editorial rules and design libraries.

The system

##### One source for every desk

Archive, newsroom standards, brand guidelines and Figma libraries, read by editors, designers and AI.

Now

##### Faster from idea to product

Every title keeps its own voice. The first new product went from concept to working prototype in days.

References

#### The same system, at any stage and any size.

Four stores in California

##### Alchemy Works

A new online shop on Shopify. The system holds the brands, the voice and every listing.

Los Angeles and Berlin

##### Concierge Coffee

Shop, wholesale and bar on the same rules, wired to Shopify and Square.

In rollout

##### A caffeinated protein bar

At Target, Costco and on a new e-commerce platform, with one identity and one set of claims in every channel.

Bags, wholesale and online

##### Apolis

Shopify, Klaviyo, Attentive and Claude connected in one system, so audience, creative and channels read from real data.

Los Angeles

##### A private trainer

A personal brand and a trainer agency, set up in the system before anything shipped.

The next step

##### A hojicha brand

Built from day one to run on the latest technology, past learnings and the system.

Beyond the brand

#### With the system in place, every unit and every person can rely on it.

- Sales and retail

- Billing

- Contracts

- Intranet

- Data

- HR

Working together

#### A quick setup, then it is simply how the company works.

##### Setup

One week to a month, depending on how digitally prepared the company is.

##### What it takes

The existing documents, a few hours of the right people, access to the tools.

##### Your data

A commercial model in your own account, or a private open-source model on your servers.

##### Coaching

Sessions with the team until working with the system is routine. Then it is kept current.

A small number of companies at a time. Say where the brand or the business should work better.

Start a conversation →

Directive Intelligence puts a company's voice, rules, facts and decisions into one system that people and AI tools work from.

## Dynaudio. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/dynaudio-art-of-listening-film.html

The Art of Listening, a Friends of Friends series for Danish speaker maker Dynaudio, with a film portrait of London designer Nicholas Daley.

Editorial · Film

"The Art of Listening."

The Art of Listening, a Friends of Friends series for Danish speaker maker Dynaudio, with a film portrait of London designer Nicholas Daley.

The Art of Listening is a collaboration between Friends of Friends and Danish speaker manufacturer Dynaudio. The series looks at individual approaches to everyday listening.

Three portraits in three cities. A sound researcher in Copenhagen. A DJ in Berlin. A fashion designer in London, whose story became the film.

01 — London

#### Music as a design tool.

Nicholas Daley designs menswear from a studio at the Bernie Grant Arts Centre in North London. His collections draw on his British-Jamaican roots and his family's musical history. His parents ran Scotland's first reggae club, in Edinburgh, in the 1970s.

A small crew travelled to London for the film. It traces his path into fashion, his work in the studio, and what listening means to him.

Music and fashion are so intertwined. One enforces the other.

02 — Berlin

#### The stereo as a shrine.

Alexandra Dröner listens at home in a loft in Prenzlauer Berg. She was one half of the DJ duo Sick Girls. In her flat the stereo is the focal point.

Music there is a singular experience. Never background noise.

03 — Copenhagen

#### Listening in public.

Holger Schulze is a professor of musicology at the University of Copenhagen. He reads a cafe as a set of sound sources. Music, a Skype call, kitchen clatter, people paying.

For him, focused listening sharpens awareness of how other people perceive the world.

Dynaudio builds loudspeakers in Denmark. For The Art of Listening, Friends of Friends produced three photographed portraits, published in spring and summer 2019.

The London story became a film portrait of Nicholas Daley, shot and edited by a reduced crew.

Live site: dynaudio.com ↗

Collaborators: FvF Productions

Völkers

Identity · Digital · Film

"The future of digital real estate presentation."

A digital-first presentation platform for one of Europe's leading real estate brokerages: rethinking how premium properties are discovered, experienced, and sold online. Built using SPOT, our proprietary asset management system.

Engel & Völkers Berlin Mitte is the most successful residential real estate location in Germany. The digital side did not show it. An outdated site, a dated identity, social and a backend that fought the people using them. Real estate is the most emotional and most expensive thing most people ever buy, and none of that was coming through online.

The work was a full digital and identity facelift, built on SPOT. It ran ahead of the brief. Engel & Völkers saw how well it performed, brought in a larger agency, and adopted the direction across the company. The new CI, the new typeface, the new website. The thinking started in Berlin.

01 — Web Design & Strategy

#### Editorial character for a premium market.

The new look reaches a younger buyer through an editorial character and strong imagery. It sets the buying impulse earlier and holds the timelessness the premium position needs.

02 — Social Media

#### A complete digital marketing system.

Social media templates, built for production, gave Engel & Völkers the tools to stand out in a market where 90% of property searches start online.

03 — Art Direction

#### Human stories for a human business.

A brand film made with Friends of Friends: a refreshed identity that holds the Hanseatic seriousness of the headquarters next to the energy of Berlin.

04 — Homes With a Story

#### Architects at home.

A content collaboration between Friends of Friends and Engel & Völkers on design and architecture. The films visit extraordinary homes and the people who built them. Here, Armand Grüntuch and Almut Grüntuch-Ernst of Grüntuch Ernst Architects walk through their buildings in Berlin.

90% of all search customers start their property search online.

Engel & Völkers Berlin Residential is one of Europe's most recognised luxury real estate brokerages. The brief was to rethink how properties are presented digitally, moving from static listings to an experience that matches the quality of the properties themselves.

The result was a digital presentation platform that leads with the visuals, cuts the friction, and reads as considered as what it shows. It performed well enough that the direction was adopted across the wider company.

## Freunde von Freunden / Friends of Friends. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/friends-of-friends-brand-identity-web.html

Freunde von Freunden, co-founded in Berlin in 2009: interview magazine, international network, books, brand productions, Berlin venues and the Friends of Friends rebrand.

Freunden

Strategy · Identity · Digital · Editorial · Event · Film

"Founded in Berlin, 2009. Renamed Friends of Friends eleven years later."

Co-founder and managing director. An interview magazine that became a company: an international network of contributors, books, a production company for brands, two venues in Berlin, events, and the rebrand as Friends of Friends.

Freunde von Freunden started in Berlin in 2009. An online interview magazine that visited creative people at home and at work, in text, photography and film. Co-founded with Tim Seifert and Torsten Bergler. The idea grew out of NoMoreSleep, the agency the founders ran at the time.

Every person portrayed came through the network. A friend, or a friend of a friend. The rule gave the magazine its name and its method.

The magazine became a company. Books, an iPad edition, mixtapes, a production company for brands, an apartment and a loft in Berlin. In 2014 about ten people worked in the Berlin office, with around 150 freelance photographers, filmmakers, producers and editors in the wider network.

01 — The magazine

#### People, at home and at work.

The core was the interview. Creatives photographed in their homes and studios, then given room to talk. No news, no gossip, no celebrity. Stories meant to stay readable for years. Berlin first, then London, New York, Los Angeles, Paris, Milan, Munich and Tokyo.

##### Two stories from the archive

freundevonfreunden.com ↗

Planted Firmly on the Ground ↗ Design, Berlin

A Discourse on Urban Landscapes ↗ Architecture, Berlin

02 — Books

#### The archive, in print.

FvF books gathered the portraits between covers. Published with Distanz, distributed worldwide by Gestalten. Volume one appeared in 2012, volume two in 2015.

03 — Network & channels

#### A community, kept in conversation.

Readers and contributors met across Facebook, Tumblr, YouTube, Instagram, Twitter and Pinterest. Each channel got its own content instead of one message pushed everywhere. More than 80 mixtapes, compiled by the team and friends, ran as a podcast and on Mixcloud.

04 — Productions for brands

#### The same eye, on commission.

An in-house production company made films and stories for brands and corporate clients, in the look of FvF. Some ran on the magazine. Others stayed internal. By 2014, partnerships with Vitra, Mercedes-Benz, Design Hotels and the Vienna Business Agency had run for two years or more.

05 — iPad edition

#### Built for the tablet.

In 2013 the magazine moved onto the iPad as its own product, not a ported website. Concept, design and development in-house at MoreSleep. A built-in video player, touch gestures, portrait and landscape reading, offline downloads. Ten interviews were free. A premium edition added book content, behind-the-scenes material and iPad-only stories. Vitra made it free at launch.

06 — Spaces & events

#### The magazine, made physical.

After years of portraying people at home, FvF opened a home of its own. The Friends Apartment launched in 2014 in Mulackstraße, Berlin-Mitte. Sixty-five square metres, two bedrooms, a full kitchen, furnished with products from partners. A venue for dinners, workshops, presentations and overnight stays.

CLOSED AW15 presentation German Press Days

Dinner with Hanya Yanagihara Hosted by Gisela Williams

#### Friends Space, Kreuzberg.

In 2016 a larger venue followed. The first floor of a 350 square metre design loft in Kreuzberg, designed with architect Philipp Mainzer. Modular architecture and furniture, a gallery lighting system, an open kitchen built with Siemens, a Sonos surround system. Productions, dinners, talks and brand events, among them a Dr. Hauschka launch event.

07 — Friends of Friends

#### A new name for an international readership.

After eleven years and almost 700 interviews, the platform relaunched as Friends of Friends. The German name had become hard to pronounce for most readers. A plain translation kept the meaning. A new identity followed: logo animation, colour, typography and motion, built to travel across editorial and social. Typefaces: Adieu by Good Type Foundry and Untitled Sans by Klim Type Foundry.

#### A new home for 700 stories.

The website was rebuilt from the ground up. A modular system let editors compose articles with unusual layouts. New interactions and a deeper search opened the full archive.

A place for sharing stories. Accessible to everybody.

Logo animation, social templates, showreel, merchandise and print. Each channel received its own content.

## Iconist. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/iconist-ipad-app.html

Iconist: a tablet-only lifestyle magazine for Welt am Sonntag's Icon supplement, built from scratch for the iPad by NoMoreSleep.

Digital · Editorial

"A tablet-only lifestyle magazine, built from scratch."

Iconist: the iPad-only lifestyle magazine for Welt am Sonntag's Icon supplement, designed and developed by Berlin agency NoMoreSleep for Axel Springer's launch of the German App Store.

Iconist grew out of Icon, the print luxury supplement of Welt am Sonntag. For the German launch of the iPad, Axel Springer's "Welt" group set out to build something beyond a digitised magazine: a tablet-only publication with content made specifically for touch.

NoMoreSleep, the Berlin design agency, built the app alongside "Welt" creative director Brian O'Connor and journalist Markus Albers. Fifteen stories were produced for the first issue, mixing product-led lifestyle content with experimental formats: filmed interviews, 360-degree room tours, and interactive image stories.

A pop-up piñata of lifestyle, fashion and culture.

01 — Designed for Touch

#### Not a magazine. An app.

Held upright, stories read in a slim single column; turned to landscape, the imagery takes over. Pop-up text layers added context to headlines, 360-degree views let readers explore rooms like the Hotel Adlon and China Club, and interactive product stories ranged from a Rolls-Royce test drive to a visit to the Boss tailoring atelier. Social sharing to Twitter and Facebook was built in from day one.

Iconist launched in 2010 as one of the first true tablet-native magazines in Germany, distinct from the wave of publisher apps that simply repackaged print pages as PDFs.

Built by NoMoreSleep for the Axel Springer "Welt" group, each quarterly issue was its own standalone app, combining product-led lifestyle journalism with formats designed specifically for the iPad.

Collaborators: Axel Springer

Welt am Sonntag

Press: Horizont ↗

kress ↗

Year: 2010

My gadgets are like the craft of ancient eras.

Anne Kjær Riechert is a social entrepreneur based in Berlin. The film moves between her home and her work.

Mick Élysée is a Congolese chef. He hosts pop-up food events around London. The film follows him at home and at work.

## LAS Art Foundation. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/las-art-foundation-brand-identity-motion.html

Art

Foundation

Strategy · Identity · Digital · Motion

"Future-thinking, bold, flexible, accessible."

A complete brand transformation for a nomadic Berlin-based art foundation: new brand architecture, visual identity, animated poster system, and a Next.js website built for artist-centred storytelling.

LAS has no fixed address. Every show lands somewhere new, which means every show has to be marketed almost from scratch. That model only works if the brand is strong enough to carry across venues and the digital side is light enough to move at the same speed.

Neither was true. The old site was outdated and so over-built that changing a button meant calling the previous agency. The work was a new brand architecture and identity flexible enough to hold any location, on a site built to be run by the people who actually run it. Artists at the centre, everywhere LAS goes.

01 — Brand Strategy & Identity

#### Future-thinking, bold, flexible, accessible.

A new brand architecture built to travel with LAS across physical and digital spaces. The identity is set in Diatype by Dinamo and Oldschool Grotesk by Kilo Type, a typographic pairing that holds the tension between the institutional and the avant-garde.

02 — Motion & Social

#### An animated identity in every channel.

Animated poster systems, social media motion templates, and digital collateral carry the new identity across all LAS touchpoints, from U-Bahn posters to Instagram stories.

03 — Digital

#### Built on Vercel, Next.js and Sanity.

The website runs on Vercel, Next.js and Sanity, built to excel in both performance and content management. Interactive hover animations through the frame system keep the site consistent with the identity at every touchpoint.

04 — Brand Guidelines & Print

#### A system built to last and travel.

Comprehensive brand guidelines ensure consistency as LAS grows: covering typography, colour, motion principles, and application across print and digital formats.

Centering the artists. Amplifying the work.

LAS Art Foundation is a nomadic Berlin-based art foundation that collaborates with artists to create large-scale experiences both online and offline. The brief was a complete brand transformation: new architecture, new identity, new digital home.

The aim was to reflect the LAS approach: future-thinking, bold, flexible, accessible. The artists sit at the centre, their faces and voices at the heart of every platform, with concise, confident communication throughout.

## Mauermuseum. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/mauermuseum-web-design.html

Website redesign for the Mauermuseum, Haus am Checkpoint Charlie, making one of Berlin's most important historical institutions accessible and navigable online.

Digital

"An intuitive website for a complex history."

Website redesign for the Mauermuseum, Haus am Checkpoint Charlie, making one of Berlin's most significant historical institutions clear, navigable, and alive online.

Since 1962, the Mauermuseum at Checkpoint Charlie has been telling the stories of people who fled East Germany and the history of the Berlin Wall.

A modular system structures the museum's complexity while responding to a constantly changing programme of events and key dates. Editorial content treatment, contemporary fonts, and a cool blue palette, informative without being stuffy.

01 — Web Design

#### Complexity, made navigable.

Visitors can buy tickets, plan their visit, and discover in-depth articles about the Berlin Wall, Checkpoint Charlie, and the museum's history, all within a device-agnostic system built to scale.

History made accessible.

Website redesign for the Mauermuseum, Checkpoint Charlie, making one of Berlin's most important historical institutions intuitively navigable online.

A modular system handling editorial content, ticket sales, event listings, and archival depth in a single coherent experience.

Live site: www.mauermuseum.de ↗

Year: 2016

## Mezcla. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/mezcla-brand-digital.html

Brand identity and website for Mezcla Gastronomía, the Argentinian restaurant group behind Casa Cavia, El Abierto, Piso Tres and ORNO.

Identity · Digital

"Chic branding for Buenos Aires’ coolest gastronomy group."

Brand identity and website for Mezcla Gastronomía, the Argentinian restaurant group behind Casa Cavia, El Abierto, Piso Tres and ORNO.

Mezcla Gastronomía is an Argentinian restaurant group whose properties are synonymous with daring and originality. Run by creative director Lupe García with her architect brother Juan Carlos, Mezcla engages a team of creative collaborators across disciplines to breathe life into spaces such as Casa Cavia, El Abierto and Piso Tres.

Mezcla needed a brand identity as inviting, lively and timeless as their restaurants. For the logo and fonts, the studio mixed the elegance of Art Deco with a subtle Latin flair, creating a look that melds naturally with each space's individual design.

Mezcla means “mixture”. Cuisine, architecture and collaborators, brought together.

The calming white expanses of the website evoke an art gallery, but they're hardly austere: six custom photo slideshows demonstrate the stunning features and unique character of each Mezcla location.

The site shows the range of the Mezcla team, from Lupe's background as a film producer to barista Daniel Calderón. It also laid the groundwork for later projects together, including ORNO.

Live site: mezclagastronomia.com ↗

Collaborators: Lupe García

Juan Carlos García

Year: 2017

## MINI. Partnership 2014–2020. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/mini-the-sooner-now-brand-campaign.html

A 2014–2020 partnership with MINI Germany and BMW: city portraits, Clubman launch content, MINI LIVING, The Sooner Now, a lookbook and sales events.

Strategy · Campaign · Editorial · Event · Film

"Exploring the future of urban living."

2014–2020 partnership with MINI Germany and BMW: city portraits, content for the Clubman launch, MINI LIVING in Milan and Los Angeles, The Sooner Now, a brand lookbook and sales events, produced with Freunde von Freunden.

MINI Germany worked with Freunde von Freunden from 2014 to 2020. It began with city guides: local creatives showed their city from the driver's seat of a MINI. It grew into portraits for the Clubman launch, coverage of MINI LIVING at design weeks in Milan and Los Angeles, and The Sooner Now, a platform, podcast and event series on the future of urban living.

Alongside the editorial work came a lookbook on the brand DNA, sales events for BMW and MINI across Germany, and work for BMW Cultural Engagement. The stories ran on Freunde von Freunden, on thesoonernow.com and on MINI channels.

##### Formats and years

2014–2016

Guided and Curated

2015–2016

01 — Guided and Curated · 2014–2016

#### A city, seen from the driver's seat.

Locals showed their city from a MINI. A chef foraging on the edge of Berlin, a photographer reading the Berlin skyline, a lamp collector at a Cologne flea market. Each portrait doubled as a guide to the places behind the work.

The series started in 2014 as city guides in five German cities and ran as Guided and Curated until 2016, with stops in Leipzig and at the Triennial of Photography in Hamburg. Several portraits from late 2015 on featured the new MINI Clubman. Stories: Dylan Watson, Noshe, Thomas Melssen.

Dylan Watson Berlin · 2015

Noshe Berlin · 2016

Thomas Melssen Cologne · 2016

02 — MINI Clubman · 2015–2016

#### Kombi. Aus nützlich und will ich.

The new MINI Clubman launched in late 2015. For the launch, three Italian workshops designed the MINI Gentleman's Collection: sunglasses by TYG in Milan, hats by Super Duper in Florence and a fragrance by Paola Bottai in Rome. Freunde von Freunden portrayed the three makers in their workshops.

In 2016 MINI Germany built its national Clubman campaign on two pairings of the useful and the desirable: the Berlin table makers Bullenberg and the New Zealand band No Wyld. Freunde von Freunden portrayed Bullenberg co-founder Albrecht von Alvensleben in 2015 and again in 2016, driving the Clubman from Berlin to the forests of Saxony-Anhalt. MINI linked the portrait from its own campaign page.

For No Wyld, the production arm FvF Productions filmed the band in New York and built the films around each member's personal story. Their track Let Me Know carried the campaign. The TV spot plays from a third-party upload. Campaign announcement: BMW Group PressClub, “Kombi. Aus nützlich und will ich.” Neue Kampagne von MINI Deutschland für den MINI Clubman startet, 2016.

03 — MINI Fashion · 2016–2017

#### Menswear in Florence.

For Pitti Uomo 90 in 2016, MINI asked five designers to reinterpret the MINI sweatshirt for its Fluid Fashion capsule collection. Freunde von Freunden portrayed Berlin designer Hien Le in Kreuzberg and covered the exhibition in Florence.

A year later, at Pitti Uomo 92, it followed the Berlin label Perret Schaad and their travel pouch for the MINI Fashion Beyond Native collection.

04 — MINI LIVING · 2016–2018

#### Small footprints, shared spaces.

MINI LIVING was the brand's architecture initiative on compact urban housing. Freunde von Freunden accompanied it from 2016: portraits of creative lead Oke Hauser in Berlin and architect Asif Khan in London, Breathe by SO – IL at the 2017 Salone del Mobile, and MINI's creative space A/D/O in Brooklyn.

At the 2018 Salone, Built by All with Studiomama proposed a micro-neighbourhood of four small units around a shared kitchen, garden and gym. Two months later the Urban Cabin, designed with FreelandBuck, stood on a downtown rooftop at the L.A. Design Festival. In Milan and Los Angeles, Freunde von Freunden covered the installations, hosted influencers and helped with invitation management.

05 — The Sooner Now: Identity · 2016–2019

#### Old and new, merged into something forward.

All branding and collateral for The Sooner Now. Posters, programmes and invitations move at the pace of city streets. The logo and type mash up serif and sans-serif styles into new letterforms.

06 — The Sooner Now: Platform, Podcast and Social

#### A platform that keeps the ideas circulating.

The events led to an online platform that keeps the ideas circulating and growing, edited by Freunde von Freunden. The Sooner Now became a monthly podcast on alternative economies, mobility, urban space and the social development of culture.

Social content and channel management ran alongside.

07 — The Sooner Now: Events

#### Conversations worth having, in cities worth knowing.

The first edition was a one-day creative conference at the new FvF Friends Space in Kreuzberg on 1 December 2016. In 2017 the format moved into dinners and panels in Munich, Stuttgart, Düsseldorf, Hamburg and Frankfurt. In 2018 it toured with design magazine IDEAT: Hamburg and Berlin in June, Düsseldorf in September, Cologne in October. In Berlin the theme was Kultur in Frauenhand, culture in women’s hands. In 2019 it held day-long festivals in Berlin and Munich.

Guests came from art, design, architecture, gastronomy and sustainability. In Berlin in 2019 a MINI Electric stood in a courtyard taped in neon yellow. Photography by Robert Rieger.

#### The series in motion.

Short films followed the editions, published on Freunde von Freunden and MINI Germany channels. From the first save-the-date to recaps of the 2018 tour and the 2019 festivals in Berlin and Munich.

## MoreSleep. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/moresleep-creative-studio.html

MoreSleep, the creative studio in Berlin and Los Angeles, co-founded in 2012. Strategy, identity, digital and campaigns for hospitality, culture and design.

Identity · Digital · Campaign

"A new model for a sleepless industry."

A creative studio in Berlin and Los Angeles. Co-founded in 2012. Two founders and a core team of designers, developers and project managers, spread across time zones.

MoreSleep opened in Berlin in 2012. The founders had already built one agency, NoMoreSleep, and seen its team move into TBWA. Freunde von Freunden was running on the side.

The second studio started from a different question. How to make exemplary work and keep the hours sustainable. The name turned the old one around.

01 — History

#### From a Berlin garden to an Echo Park rooftop.

The founders met in Berlin in 2005. NoMoreSleep followed in 2006, a digital agency and production studio. Freunde von Freunden started in 2009 as a side project.

In 2010 TBWA acquired NoMoreSleep. That story has its own page. MoreSleep opened in 2012. Friends Space opened in 2016. A Kreuzberg office followed in 2017, a Los Angeles office in Echo Park in 2020.

The founders meet in Berlin 2005

NoMoreSleep founded 2006

Freunde von Freunden starts 2009

TBWA acquires NoMoreSleep 2010

Friends Space opens 2016

Kreuzberg office 2017

02 — Offer

#### Strategy first. Then everything it needs.

Strategy and narrative. Concept. Brand transformation. Digital design and development. Content. Campaigns.

Design and engineering in one team. SPOT, an in-house asset management system, grew out of years of client builds. Collaborations and equity models sit next to classic client work.

03 — Values

#### Five values, each given an object.

Trust. Nobody knows everything, so talent gets pooled. Time. Used well, saved where possible. Curiosity. Questions lead to better ways of working.

Lasting. Beauty is good, usefulness lasts longer. Fun. Work worth doing can be fun to do. Each value got its own carrier: a flag, a cap, a newspaper, a laptop screen, a wrist.

04 — Culture

#### An office in Kreuzberg, one in Echo Park, many kitchen tables.

Remote from the first day. A team spread across cities and time zones, meeting in Berlin and Los Angeles. Self-starters who run their own projects and clients.

Projects stay open for input from anyone in the studio. Unlimited holidays. The best lines from the team chat ended up as a sticker set.

Los Angeles office, Echo Park 2020

05 — In-house

#### Briefs from inside the studio.

Summer 2019 marked the tenth summer party, shared with Friends of Friends. The give-away shirt set the two studios in two typefaces, with date, time and place printed on the back.

The 2019 Christmas present to the team was a shirt with wishes for 2020. More fun, more time, more friends, more music, more books, more freedom.

## NoMoreSleep × TBWA. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/nomoresleep-tbwa-digital-arts.html

In 2010 TBWA acquired NoMoreSleep for its Berlin Digital Arts group, as TBWA Germany set out to make the whole agency digital.

× TBWA

Digital · Transformation

"A digital agency moves inside a network agency."

In 2010 TBWA acquired NoMoreSleep for its Berlin Digital Arts group. The brief was to make the whole agency digital, not to add a digital unit next to it.

NoMoreSleep started in Berlin in 2006. A digital agency and production studio. One of its builds was Iconist, an iPad-only magazine for the Welt group at Axel Springer.

Four years in, TBWA acquired the agency.

01 — Context

#### Where digital sat in 2010.

Network agencies in Germany were deciding how to handle digital. Some kept it in separate sister companies. TBWA ran a digital-only agency in other markets and chose not to open it in Germany.

TBWA Germany went the other way. The plan was to digitise the whole agency, starting in Berlin.

02 — The deal

#### An acquisition, ten people.

In August 2010 TBWA acquired NoMoreSleep. Ten people moved over to TBWA Berlin, the founders among them.

The team joined the Digital Arts group. Terms were not made public.

03 — The transformation

#### Digital inside the core agency.

Digital Arts sat inside the core agency, not next to it. After the move, about a fifth of the roughly 80 people in the Berlin office had a digital background. Berlin was set up as the model for the Hamburg and Düsseldorf offices to follow.

Iconist, built by NoMoreSleep 2010

MoreSleep opens 2012

04 — Outcomes

#### Then a new studio.

MoreSleep opened in Berlin in 2012, with a model built around remote work and sustainable hours.

In 2010 TBWA acquired NoMoreSleep and brought its team into the Berlin Digital Arts group. TBWA Germany planned Berlin as the model for building digital into the core agency.

MoreSleep followed in 2012.

Co-founders: Torsten Bergler

Thomas Michelbach

Press: HORIZONT ↗

kress ↗

Year: 2010

## NOMOS Glashütte. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/nomos-at-work-film-series.html

Nomos at Work, a Friends of Friends series for NOMOS Glashütte on the changing nature of work, with portraits and films in Berlin, New York and San Francisco.

Editorial · Film

"Nomos at Work."

Nomos at Work, a Friends of Friends series for NOMOS Glashütte on the changing nature of work, with portraits and films in Berlin, New York and San Francisco.

NOMOS Glashütte builds mechanical watches in a small town in Saxony. Nomos at Work looked at a question outside the watch world: what does work mean today, and what will it mean tomorrow? Each story asked about success, vision and status, told from the places where people work and live.

Friends of Friends developed the editorial concept and led the research. FvF Productions sourced the protagonists from its network and developed the video narrative. Three portraits in three cities, two of them also as films.

##### Formats and years

October 2017

Berlin

Film and photo story with a coworking pioneer

November 2017 · February 2018

New York

Photo story, then film, with a home design founder

December 2017

San Francisco

Photo story with an agency partner

01 — Berlin · 2017

#### New work, on a small scale.

Ansgar Oberholz opened St. Oberholz at Rosenthaler Platz in 2005. It was the first cafe in Berlin built around freelancers, founders and their laptops. SoundCloud and HelloFresh started at its tables. He later co-founded the Institut für Neue Arbeit and advises companies on how they work.

The film and the photo story follow him through Mitte. The cafe and its coworking floors, a quiet garrison cemetery, a fab lab and the office of Moebel Horzon.

##### Ansgar Oberholz

Read the story on Friends of Friends ↗

New work can also happen on a small scale.

02 — New York · 2017–2018

#### A home worth coming back to.

Tariq Dixon co-founded TRNK, an online shop for home design, with Nick Nemechek. Both had worked as menswear buyers. Their showroom in NoHo is set up like an apartment and doubles as the office.

The episode was shot in New York. The crew filmed at his Brooklyn apartment, the showroom and the studio of a ceramicist who makes pieces for TRNK. The photo story ran in November 2017, the film followed in February 2018.

##### Tariq Dixon

Read the story on Friends of Friends ↗

03 — San Francisco · 2017

#### Just strategy.

Michael Martin is a managing partner at Code and Theory and leads its West Coast office. The agency designs publishing platforms for media companies such as Bloomberg, The Verge and the BBC.

The San Francisco portrait ran as a photo story. It moves from his apartment in Jackson Square through Chinatown to the agency office on Maiden Lane.

##### Michael Martin

Read the story on Friends of Friends ↗

There’s no such thing as a digital strategy; it’s just strategy.

Three portraits of people who shape how work looks today. A coworking pioneer, a home design founder and an agency partner.

The stories ran on Friends of Friends in English and German between October 2017 and February 2018. FvF Productions directed and shot both films.

## ORNO. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/orno-pizza-branding.html

Branding and web design for ORNO, a Buenos Aires pizzeria from Mezcla Gastronomía reinterpreting Neapolitan pizza with a Miami Art Deco edge.

Identity · Digital

"Communicating the fire and passion of Argentine pizza."

Branding and web design for ORNO, a Buenos Aires pizzeria from Mezcla Gastronomía reinterpreting Neapolitan pizza with a Miami Art Deco edge.

ORNO is a restaurant from Argentina's Mezcla Gastronomía that interprets classic Neapolitan pizza using the finest local ingredients. At its heart is the Forni Grimaldi, a 400-degree traditional pizza oven, with every pie made in full view of guests.

The interior mixes modernist shapes in vibrant pastels, a chic update on Miami Art Deco that's the opposite of a traditional pizzeria. Based on a sharing concept, the oven takes centre stage and the entire space echoes its basic geometry.

The heat of the oven, at the heart of the brand.

The identity uses geometric, basic shapes with a contrasting red logo that symbolises ORNO's core: the heat of their pizza oven. Working closely with the Mezcla team, the studio ideated and produced all collateral in the space, from exterior signage to stickers to pizza boxes.

The website follows the same look and feel: a simple one-page design with easy navigation, strong photography and insight into the local producers behind ORNO's pizza.

Live site: ornopizzeria.com ↗

Collaborators: Mezcla Gastronomía

Year: 2019

## PURO Hotels. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/puro-hotels-brand-identity.html

Visual identity and branding for Magari and Loreta, the restaurant and rooftop bar at PURO Hotels' Warsaw location.

Identity

"A stylish twist for Warsaw’s latest destination."

Visual identity and branding for Magari and Loreta, the restaurant and rooftop bar at PURO Hotels' Warsaw location.

PURO is a boutique hotel group in Poland. The studio was asked to create the visual identity and branding for the restaurant and rooftop bar of their Warsaw location: two complementary yet individual destinations that reflect the modern elegance of the PURO hotels.

Magari, whose name means “What if?” in Italian, is a friendly, family-oriented restaurant tapping into la dolce vita with modern Italian dishes and locally-sourced, seasonal produce. Inspired by the brightness and architecture of coastal Italy, the branding uses a sunny colour palette and playful imagery.

Two destinations, one address, two distinct moods.

Loreta is a rooftop bar with an impressive cocktail menu and an even more impressive view over Warsaw. The studio tapped into its midcentury-modern-meets-tropical interior and cozy vibe with bold typefaces and a millennial chic palette of light pink and hot red.

Together, Magari and Loreta give PURO's Warsaw location two complementary identities, each branded down to the coasters and menu covers.

Live site: purohotel.pl ↗

Year: 2019

## QWSTION. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/qwstion-company-portrait.html

A company portrait of QWSTION, the Zurich bag brand behind Bananatex, filmed at their studio and headquarters.

Editorial · Film

"Inside the Zurich studio rethinking sustainable bags."

A company portrait of QWSTION, the Zurich bag brand behind Bananatex, filmed at their studio and headquarters.

Look behind the curtain at the creative laboratory and headquarters of Swiss bag brand QWSTION in Zurich and you'll find a work in progress: industrial sewing machines, prototypes in development, and a team debating sustainability, functionality and design.

Friends of Friends produced a company portrait exploring QWSTION's approach to materials, from early experiments with organic cotton to Bananatex, their proprietary fabric made from banana-plant fibre, open-sourced for the wider industry to use.

Plants, not plastic.

Founded in Zurich in 2008, QWSTION makes bags and accessories designed for longevity, built from natural and recycled materials. Their Bananatex fabric, made from abacá fibre grown in the Philippines, is fully biodegradable and open-source.

Friends of Friends filmed a company portrait at QWSTION's Zurich studio and store, part of an ongoing editorial conversation about sustainability, functionality and design.

Live site: qwstion.com ↗

## Ritz-Carlton Berlin. Frederik Frede

A Roaring Twenties gala reopens the Ritz-Carlton Berlin: concept, production and art direction by MoreSleep.

Event · Campaign

A Roaring Twenties gala reopens the Ritz-Carlton Berlin.

For the grand reopening of the Ritz-Carlton Berlin, a Roaring Twenties-inspired Golden Gala was concepted and produced end to end: PR, artist programming, invitations, interior decoration, production and styling. Over 1,000 celebrities and VIPs attended, 500 bottles of champagne were poured, 7 artists performed.

The Ritz-Carlton Berlin is Marriott's signature address in Europe, the one the group points to. It had just come through a full interior renovation of every facility. The building was new again. The brand around it was not. The assets, the tone, the audience still read older than the rooms now did.

The work rebranded and redesigned every Berlin hospitality outlet across the property, restaurants and bars included, then put a Roaring Twenties Golden Gala on top of it to carry the relaunch. Built to set the property back in front of a younger, cultural Berlin, and to make the reopening an event people wanted to be at, not an announcement they received.
