Brand identity and website for Roterfaden, an independent German maker of premium handcrafted personal planners, an online experience as well-crafted as their products.

Identity · E-Commerce

"Digital craft for handmade objects."

Brand identity refresh and website for Roterfaden, an independent German maker of premium handcrafted personal planners.

ROTERFADEN makes premium handcrafted personal organisers, the Taschenbegleiter, in Germany. 100% independent. The brief was to build an online experience as beautiful and well-considered as the products themselves.

The website was designed from a user-first perspective: highly visual, curated, more boutique than shop. The homepage makes space for the brand to breathe, with dedicated storytelling pages covering values and sustainability.

01 — Identity

#### Stamp evolution.

An updated visual identity that respects the brand's craft heritage. Logo refinement, typography, and a tightened colour system, all developed to sit naturally alongside the tactility of the products.

02 — Art Direction

#### Light, shade, and material.

Updated product and editorial photography to bring out the tactility of Roterfaden's work. The photography treatment translates the physical craft of the products into the digital experience.

03 — E-Commerce

#### Immersion in the product.

Product overview pages are modular and customisable. Users can explore individual products in detail before selecting variants, the feeling of the shop mirrors the care that goes into the planners.

The feel of a curated boutique.

A brand identity refresh and new website for ROTERFADEN, the independent German maker of premium handcrafted personal planners.

## Ruinart × Jeppe Hein. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/ruinart-jeppe-hein-carte-blanche.html

Film direction and production for Ruinart's Carte Blanche 2022 with artist Jeppe Hein, capturing the multi-sensory installation 'Right Here, Right Now'.

Jeppe Hein

Film

"Right Here, Right Now."

Film direction and production for Ruinart's Carte Blanche 2022, following Danish artist Jeppe Hein from the Maison's vineyards and chalk cellars to the multi-sensory installation "Right Here, Right Now."

Each year Ruinart hands its Carte Blanche to an artist for a fresh interpretation of the Maison's history and savoir-faire. For 2022, Danish artist Jeppe Hein translated his visit to Ruinart's vineyards, bottling plant and chalk cellars in Reims into a short film series and a participatory installation.

Direction and production followed Hein through the vineyards and cellars, capturing the textures, colours and rituals that became the raw material for "Right Here, Right Now". A piece built around the four elements at the heart of champagne making.

01 — Right Here, Right Now

#### A film built around the senses.

"The essential idea of my work is trying to open up your heart," Hein says in the film. The series follows him through the maison, working with chalk, mirrors and grapes, the same elements visitors encounter in the installation itself.

I experienced at Ruinart a sense of awareness, a sense of nature.

"Right Here, Right Now" travelled from the Palais de Tokyo to the Venice Biennale, Frieze, Art Basel and beyond. A participatory installation summoning earth, water, air and fire, the elements essential to champagne making.

The accompanying film, shot on location at Maison Ruinart, set the tone for the campaign across its international tour and the Berlin Gallery Weekend pop-up restaurant with chef Björn Swanson.

Live site: jeppehein.ruinart.com ↗

Collaborators: Jeppe Hein

Year: 2022

## Schattenfinder. Frederik Frede

Website and interactive product advisor for Schattenfinder, a sunshade platform for over 100 solutions from five German manufacturers.

Website and interactive product advisor for Schattenfinder, a sunshade platform built with leading German manufacturers.

01 — Platform

#### Everything in one place.

Over 100 customisable solutions from five manufacturers. The backend runs on SPOT, a custom asset management system. All product data and filter logic come from one data source.

Landing pages and questionnaire share the same flexible structure.

02 — Product advisor

#### Not sure which solution fits?

An interactive advisor points users to the right categories and products. A short quiz asks about requirements and mounting options.

Two parts allow very granular filtering. Everything stays in sync with the central data in SPOT.

03 — Powered by SPOT

#### Asset management, simplified.

SPOT was built by MoreSleep and ENGN. A leaner, more affordable answer to the cost and complexity of asset management systems. Files stay together, current and easy to check.

More on SPOT.

Website and product advisor for Schattenfinder. Over 100 sunshade solutions, one data source, a few questions to the right product.

## Siemens. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/siemens-home-appliances.html

Content partnership with Siemens Home Appliances, 2015–2019: Home Stories, Culinary Encounters, Architect Dialogues and the Friends Space kitchen.

Editorial · Film

Home appliances, kitchens and the people who live with them.

2015–2019 content partnership: home films, chef portraits, architect interviews and a Siemens kitchen in the Friends Space, produced by Friends of Friends across Europe, Asia and Australia.

Siemens Home Appliances sells to a mass market. Its ovens and fridges are reliable and easy to overlook. A younger, design-minded audience rarely thinks about the brand until the day it plans a kitchen. The partnership set out to reach that audience earlier, inside the homes and kitchens it already admired.

Friends of Friends produced the work from 2015 to 2019. It began with three home portraits in Berlin and grew into four formats: documentary home films in seven cities, a chef series in four, an interview series with architects, and a Siemens kitchen built into the Friends Space in Kreuzberg. The films ran on Friends of Friends and on Siemens channels. FRAME and Baumeister carried select interviews.

##### Formats and years

2015–2018

Home Stories

Nine homes, seven cities, ten films

2019

Culinary Encounters

Four chefs in Oslo, Paris, Berlin and Maastricht

2019

Architect Dialogues

Four architects in Berlin, Paris, Amsterdam and Helsinki

2016–2018

Built-in Kitchen

A campaign kitchen shaped by four creatives, built into the Friends Space in Kreuzberg

01 — Home Stories · 2015–2018

#### Innovative living, in real homes.

Home Stories looked at urban living through the people who shape it: architects, gallerists and makers in unusual homes. Each film shows the space and the life inside it, kitchen included. The series opened in 2015 with three Berlin portraits: a former lingerie factory, a houseboat and a 1950s gas station. It travelled on to London, Stockholm, Antwerp, Melbourne, Hong Kong and the Dutch countryside until 2018.

02 — Culinary Encounters · 2019

#### Four kitchens, four cities.

Culinary Encounters followed four young chefs in Oslo, Paris, Berlin and Maastricht and asked how a new generation approaches food, kitchen culture and new recipes. Each chef was filmed and interviewed in their own city and kitchen. Filmed in 2018.

The series ran in two parts. The home portraits ran on Friends of Friends from February to April 2019. The kitchen films brought each chef to the Friends Space in Berlin to cook one dish in the Siemens kitchen, and ran on Siemens channels from March 2019.

03 — Architect Dialogues · 2019

#### Design philosophies, four cities.

Architect Dialogues was an interview series with award-winning architects and interior designers in Berlin, Paris, Amsterdam and Helsinki. Each conversation took place in their homes or studios and covered design philosophy, urban living and the challenges facing cities. Extended versions ran on the Siemens Home Appliances site. FRAME and Baumeister carried select interviews to their readers.

04 — Built-in Kitchen · 2016–2018

#### A kitchen built to bring people together.

The Friends Space is the physical home of Friends of Friends: a 350 sqm loft in Kreuzberg, designed with architect Philipp Mainzer and opened in 2016. Its kitchen is a collaboration with Siemens Home Appliances. Black built-in units, an induction hob with integrated extraction and an open layout make it work for cooking classes, dinner presentations and film shoots.

The kitchen came out of the Built-in Kitchen campaign for Siemens. Four creatives from four countries shaped it: designers Anna-Riika and Katriina Nuutinen in Helsinki, chef Jos Timmer in Amsterdam, photographer Fabrice Fouillet in Paris and kitchen designer Andrea Balonier in Berlin. Portrait films show each of them at home, talking about the kitchen they need. The case film follows the process from sketches and planning to factory visits and installation in the Friends Space.

The kitchen served as a set for the partnership. The Culinary Encounters chefs cooked their dishes there for the kitchen films. It also hosted the wider network: supper clubs such as Clam Club, brand dinners for up to 120 guests, and productions for other clients.

## Signal LA. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/signal-la-brand-identity.html

Brand identity for an architectural retail enclave in the Los Angeles Arts District: identity system, print, signage, merch, and digital.

LA

Identity · Digital · Campaign

An architectural retail enclave

in the Arts District.

Brand identity for Signal, a curated multi-brand retail destination at 821 Traction Avenue, Los Angeles, bringing together design, fashion, and culture under one roof.

Signal is a curated retail enclave in Los Angeles's Arts District, uniting a constellation of independent brands under a shared architectural identity, from Alchemy Works and Flamingo Estate to Period Correct and Please Do Not Enter. The brief called for a brand language that could hold its own against the building's presence: quiet authority, deep green, and a typographic system rooted in editorial publishing.

The identity draws on the language of place: an address, a directory, a signal. The wordmark occupies space the way a building does, without apology. Applied across print, signage, merch, and digital, the system scales from a pavement A-frame to a full-bleed website hero without losing its composure.

01 — Brand Identity

#### Typography as architecture.

A high-contrast serif wordmark anchored in deep forest green. The identity operates as a directory system. The tenants are listed as typographic content, turning the who into the what. Consistent across every surface, the system reads as institutional without feeling corporate.

02 — Print & Signage

#### The pavement is part of the brand.

The A-frame sandwich board extends the identity into the street: a deep green field, the wordmark at full bleed, the tenant directory as body copy. Poster formats follow the same logic: the SIGNAL masthead as editorial cover, tenant names as content, the building's address as provenance.

03 — Merchandise

#### Wearable wayfinding.

The t-shirt extends the directory logic into merch. The full tenant list prints in small-cap text beneath the wordmark, turning the garment into a walking map of the enclave. Tone-on-tone in Signal green: legible to those who know, invisible to those who don't.

04 — Digital

#### The address as the homepage.

The website carries the same editorial logic as print: the wordmark centred, the address as coordinates, the tenant directory as navigation. Photography takes over where typography ends, the building's arched facades and light-filled interiors doing the rest of the work.

A brand that behaves like a building.

Signal is a multi-brand retail destination at 821 Traction Avenue in Los Angeles's Arts District, bringing together a curated selection of independent brands in design, fashion, and culture. The identity system was built to match the architectural ambition of the space: a mark with the permanence of an address and the flexibility of a publishing platform.

Live site: signal-la.com ↗

Collaborators: Klein Agency

Maša Kleinhample

Jon Kleinhample

Year: 2023

## Sonos. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/sonos-listening-better-brand-activation.html

Sonos work with Friends of Friends, 2016 to 2018: a Berlin home film, an in-home story series, an IFA press hub and the HAY x Sonos One launch.

Campaign · Editorial · Event · Film

Listening better, told across formats.

Sonos work with Friends of Friends, 2016 to 2018: a Berlin home film, an in-home story series, an IFA press hub and the HAY x Sonos One launch.

From 2016 to 2018, Friends of Friends worked with Sonos on one idea: music changes how a home feels. The work ran across film, editorial, events and product.

A short film opened a Berlin home to the Sonos and Apple Music campaign Music Makes It Home. Eight in-home stories followed, from Hamburg to Kent. At IFA 2018, a press hub in Berlin launched the Sonos Amp. The HAY x Sonos One edition took the speaker into design retail and onto shelves across social media.

01 — IFA listening hub, 2018

#### A press hub for IFA Berlin.

IFA is Europe's largest consumer electronics show. Away from the halls, an external hub at Zwei Drei Raum gave global press and industry an early look at the Sonos Amp and other new products.

Scope covered concept, location sourcing, styling, catering and music, through to execution. Project page on Friends of Friends ↗

02 — In-home stories, 2017–2018

#### Sound, space and creative practice.

An in-home video and editorial series by FvF Productions for Sonos, launched as Wake Up The Silent Home. Talent came from the FvF network: illustrators, musicians, tattoo artists and designers. Every visit asked the same questions. Which music shaped a life? What plays at home today?

Eight stories across five countries, each shot in the subject's own space, with the speakers part of the room.

## SPOT. Asset Management System. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/spot-asset-management-system.html

SPOT: a proprietary asset management system developed by MoreSleep, centralising marketing data across channels and clients.

Digital

"Centralise your data, so it's all in one Spot."

A proprietary asset management system developed in-house at MoreSleep: built to centralise marketing data, streamline workflows, and power client-facing digital products across multiple channels.

SPOT is an Asset Management System designed and optimised with decades of digital experience. Built to serve as the single source of truth for all marketing assets and channels: replacing a wild and asynchronous mix of systems with one powerful, flexible platform.

Developed in partnership with ENGN, SPOT has been deployed across multiple client environments, proving its versatility from internal brand asset tools to full client-facing product platforms.

01 — The System

#### No more folders. No more lost files.

SPOT is your virtual filing cabinet: easily sort, categorise, and access assets with a few clicks. Share, collaborate, and exchange with team members effortlessly. No more emailing large files or losing track of feedback. One system for all your marketing cases and channels.

02 — Markilux & Schattenfinder

#### From internal tool to client-facing platform.

For Markilux, we built an internal solution for assets management, which they then extended into Schattenfinder, a client-facing product platform allowing data from different brands to flow from a single, unified source. One system, two expressions.

03 — Engel & Völkers

#### Real estate assets, unified across locations.

For long-standing client Engel & Völkers, SPOT enabled the first step towards transforming how they manage real estate assets across different locations, a scalable system that grows with their business.

One system. Every asset. All your channels.

SPOT was conceived and built by MoreSleep as a proprietary platform: the result of years of building bespoke digital solutions for clients and recognising the need for a unified, flexible system that could sit at the centre of any brand's marketing operation.

Available to clients as a standalone product or integrated into broader digital engagements.

Live site: spotsystem.de ↗

Collaborators: ENGN

Year: 2020–present

Three Creative Paths: a Friends of Friends film and editorial series for Squarespace with three Berlin founders who built a career online, 2022.

Logo, identity and website for Swayed, an AI platform helping hospitality clients deliver next-level service, balancing advanced technology with human warmth.

## Thonet. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/thonet-brand-narrative.html

Brand narrative and editorial direction for Thonet: one of the oldest furniture brands in the world, inventors of the bentwood chair, and a cornerstone of modern design history.

Strategy · Editorial

"175 years of design, retold."

Brand narrative and editorial direction for Thonet: one of the oldest furniture brands in the world, inventors of the bentwood chair, and a cornerstone of modern design history.

Thonet has been making furniture since 1819: they invented the bentwood chair, shaped the Viennese café, and produced some of the most widely recognised objects in design history. With over 175 years of heritage, the challenge was finding the contemporary voice that honours that legacy without being imprisoned by it.

We developed a brand narrative strategy that frames Thonet not as a museum piece but as a living design practice, connecting their historical innovation to contemporary design culture.

175 years of design, retold.

Thonet has been making furniture since 1819: they invented the bentwood chair, shaped the Viennese café, and produced some of the most widely recognised objects in design history. With over 175 years of heritage, the challenge was finding the contemporary voice that honours that legacy without being imprisoned by it.

We developed a brand narrative strategy that frames Thonet not as a museum piece but as a living design practice, connecting their historical innovation to contemporary design culture.

## Umane. Brand Identity. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/umane-brand-identity.html

A modern performance brand built for ambition, driven by purpose. Strategy, identity, and design system for Umane, a holistic wellness club in Berlin.

Strategy · Identity · Digital · AI · Consulting

"Built for movement, shaped by care."

A modern performance brand for a Berlin wellness club built for ambition and driven by purpose. Naming rationale through to full design system: strategy, identity, motion, and application.

Umane began as BAC, Berlin Athletic Club. A name that works for one room in one city and quietly caps the business there. Put Berlin in the name and national or international growth turns awkward fast, the way Design Miami Basel reads once it travels. BAC on its own says nothing to someone who has not been told what it stands for. The ambition was bigger than the name could hold.

Umane fixed that at the root. A name that scales, with care and the human built into it, then the whole brand around it. Naming rationale, strategy, six pillars, visual identity, typography, the colour, gradient and texture systems, motion, and a full set of templates across web, keynote, and social. Built so a place with real ambition could open already looking like it knew exactly what it was, anywhere it went next.

01 — Brand Strategy

#### Performance is not a spike. It is a way of living.

The strategic foundation rests on six pillars, with Capability as Culture at its centre. Umane doesn't sell better workouts. It builds a culture that lives better. The brand reframes performance: from pressure to presence, from competition to care, from hustle to real capability. Science, design, and humanity made visible in everything built.

#### Built with Claude, from the first brief.

This is the first MoreSleep project developed entirely in collaboration with Claude, not as an execution tool but as a thinking partner from day one. Strategy, naming rationale, brand pillars, tone of voice, design system logic, art direction: all iterated in conversation, decisions pressure-tested against the brand's own logic in real time. The deliverable came in two layers: a human-facing system (identity, guidelines, this case study) and a structured brand system of YAML and Markdown files defining positioning, voice, and visual tokens, readable by both people and agents. Same brand, two formats. Built for how teams actually work today.

We don't sit still. We shape.

02 — Logo

#### A wordmark built from circles.

The Umane logo is the visual cornerstone of the identity: each letterform constructed from overlapping circles, echoing the brand's core forms: the human body in motion, the dot pattern system, the gradient language. A lock-up system extends the wordmark across sub-brands. Club, Foods, Health, Coach each share the same modular logic.

03 — Typography

#### Geometric precision and human warmth.

Milling Duplex brings geometric precision to headlines. Tiempos brings warmth and clarity to body copy. Together they reflect the brand's duality: evidence-based and human-centred. The type system plays with scale, weight, and contrast, from cinematic single-word statements to dense editorial body text.

04 — Colour

#### Restrained, warm, and tactile.

Color is restrained with neutral foundations punctuated by thoughtful accents. Soft backgrounds create calm and healing. Energetic contrasts in cyan, mint, and yellow motivate and activate. Every palette decision serves both the body and the mind.

Black

Off-white

Healing Blue

Pale Green

Sand

Cyan

Mint

Yellow

05 — Design System

#### The circle organises in three key ways.

Logo grid, marker shapes, gradient language, dot texture: one unified toolkit. Applied across web, app, social, and print. The system is modular: it moves, breathes, and organises. Designed not to impress, but to resonate. Every element intentional, every application systematic.

06 — Art Direction

#### The poetry of physical intelligence.

Umane's visual language captures how the body interacts with gravity, light, and space. Every frame embodies presence, precision, and natural rhythm, revealing the quiet power of human movement. The focus is on authentic motion, not performance, on how movement feels, not just how it looks. Matte textures, monochrome, natural fibers. Studios with character. The body as landscape.

07 — Applications

#### A brand that lives on every surface.

From supplement tins and sachets to washi tape and tote bags, social content to digital UI. The identity system scales across every touchpoint without losing its logic. Each application demonstrates the same modular thinking: the circle, the wordmark, the gradient, the dot. Different surface, same brand.

08 — Website

#### A digital home built on the same logic.

The website carries the full identity system into a working digital product. Wordmark, type hierarchy, gradient language, dot texture, and marker system all translated into layout and interaction. Built on Framer, the site applies the brand's restraint: editorial hierarchy, minimal UI, the body as the primary visual. Strength & Conditioning, Physiotherapy, Nutrition, Performance Lab, all built on rhythm, clarity, and capability.

Capability, calibrated.

Umane is a holistic wellness club in Berlin, renamed from BAC, Berlin Athletic Club, to a name built to scale. The full project ran from strategy through design system: brand positioning, naming rationale, six strategic pillars, tone of voice, visual identity (logo, lock-up system), typography (Milling Duplex + Tiempos), colour palette, gradient system, texture language, art direction, motion principles, and applications across digital, social, and print.

The visual language is built on balance. Clarity and character at once, structure carrying softness. Every element modular and intentional. The result reads as intelligent, grounded, and quietly aspirational, a direct line back to the brand's promise: capability, calibrated.

Live site: umane.com ↗

Collaborators: Emely Wensky

Sveta Koliada

Claude (Anthropic)

Year: 2024 · 2025

## USM Modular Furniture. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/usm-modular-furniture-brand-digital.html

A multi-channel editorial platform, Personalities by USM, showcasing how individuals relate to and style their USM furniture, with a 192-page hardcover book published by Hatje Cantz.

Modular

Furniture

Editorial · Campaign

"The interior life of inanimate objects."

A multi-channel editorial platform, Personalities by USM, showcasing how individuals relate to and style their USM furniture, with a 192-page hardcover book published by Hatje Cantz.

USM makes some of the most quietly radical furniture of the last sixty years. In Germany it had drifted into something else: the furniture of law firms, clinics, the family home. Practical. Permanent. Not design. The Haller system was a modernist benchmark and the audience speccing it was aging, while a younger design crowd looked straight past it. There was almost no digital presence to argue otherwise.

Personalities by USM answered the perception, not the product. Real people, real homes, showing how they actually live with the system. The work moved USM from a catalogue object back into a design object, in the places where taste gets formed.

01 — Personalities by USM

#### The interior life of inanimate objects.

Personalities is a multi-channel editorial platform: a contemporary interview series profiling exceptional people from fashion, architecture, design, art and culture in cooperation with Freunde von Freunden. Published monthly, each instalment features a notable personality who has made USM the furniture of choice for their private or professional environment. The project spanned a dedicated website, a nationwide German event series, and a 192-page hardcover book published by Hatje Cantz.

01b — The Book

#### 192 pages. 16 personalities. 13 photographers.

The most compelling portraits and interviews were collated into a 192-page full-colour hardcover book published by Hatje Cantz: released October 2015 and launched at Frankfurter Buchmesse alongside a nationwide Germany tour. An exclusive Ape carrying a curated bookshop toured Frankfurt, Hamburg and Berlin, with launch events at saasfee* pavillon, 25hours HafenCity and the FvF Apartment.

01c — project50

#### Fifty years of Haller, rethought by students.

For the 50th anniversary of the Haller system, USM invited design students worldwide to rethink modularity, and the results were celebrated with FvF and BLESS in the Münzstudio apartment in Berlin Mitte.

02 — Content Production & Social Media

#### Eight years. 224,000+ followers. Built from zero.

Friends of Friends managed all international social media accounts for USM across Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and Pinterest: developing strategy, producing content, and organising launch events. Over eight years the following grew from near zero, reached 1.9 million unique accounts, achieved 310% Instagram growth since 2019, and held a 5.24% average engagement rate.

224,000+ followers · 1.9M unique accounts reached · 310% Instagram growth · 5.24% avg. engagement rate

03 — Website Strategy & Pitch

#### A €512,000 vision they built without us.

In 2020 a comprehensive pitch proposed a full relaunch of usm.com: UX strategy, complete UI redesign, new information architecture, integrated e-commerce, and SPOT as the central CMS and DAM. The audit named the core problems: too complex for users, poor SEO, an inconsistent system, costly maintenance. The proposal answered them with a modular, brand-aligned, editorially-driven platform. USM did not commission the project, but the ideas that carried into their later website rebuild were core to what the pitch laid out.

03b — SPOT as CMS

#### One system for all data, all channels, all markets.

At the heart of the pitch was SPOT, our proprietary asset management system developed with ENGN, proposed as the single platform for all USM content, product data, translations and digital outputs across all markets.

04 — The WorkHouse

#### Six weeks in the Berlin countryside.

In June 2018, USM transformed the historic “Wehrmühle Biesenthal” estate north of Berlin into The WorkHouse: a six-week live-work laboratory developed with Dutch architecture firm UNStudio. The full event concept, guest management, speaker programme, and media and influencer communications for the opening weekend and residency ran through the studio.

04b — Open House

#### International speakers, interactive installations, residency.

The opening weekend brought together international experts for talks, interactive installations, and workshops. During the residency period, guests could book one of six rooms in exchange for leaving behind their vision of the future of work. Concept, speakers, guests, press, and on-site production all ran through the studio.

05 — Journey of a Product

#### From Swiss manufactory to home delivery.

A short documentary follows a single USM Haller shelf from purchase through manufacturing at USM's Swiss headquarters to delivery and assembly in a customer's home, offering a transparent look at the process behind the brand's modular system.

USM is a Swiss designer and manufacturer of high-end modular furniture. The Haller system has been a benchmark of modernist design since the 1960s. Personalities by USM is a multi-channel platform showing how individuals relate to and style their USM products.

Made with Friends of Friends, the editorial strategy and digital roll-out paired curated portraits of each Personality in their space with in-depth interviews on their aesthetic and their views on design. The strongest stories were gathered into a 192-page full-colour hardcover published with Hatje Cantz.

Live site: www.personalities-by-usm.com ↗

Collaborators: Friends of Friends

## Visit California. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/visit-california-dream-big-portraits.html

Friends of Friends portraits of Californians for Visit California's Dream Big campaign, with a short film on Ventura photographer Dylan Gordon.

Editorial · Film · Campaign

"Lives shaped by the coast."

Friends of Friends portraits of Californians for Visit California's Dream Big campaign, with a short film on Ventura photographer Dylan Gordon.

Dream Big was the brand campaign of Visit California. For it, Friends of Friends profiled people based in California whose lives are shaped by the coast and the outdoors.

A photographer in Ventura. An interactive art director in Silicon Valley. Three brothers behind a fashion label in Los Angeles. The Ventura story also became a short documentary, conceived, directed and produced by FvF Productions.

01 — Ventura

#### All summer in a day.

Dylan Gordon photographs surfing, skating and motorcycles. He is on the road for most of the year. Ventura is where he comes back to, a coastal town with a close community of surfers, photographers and filmmakers.

The film packs a whole summer into one day. An early surf at Surfers Point. A motorcycle ride inland to a swimming hole in the mountains around Ojai. A campfire with friends.

His studio is a converted mechanic's warehouse. He shoots Polaroids there and makes books and zines, prints meant to outlast a feed.

Read the story on Freunde von Freunden ↗

There's no ego and no competition in Ventura.

02 — Sunnyvale

#### California Modern.

Stefan Schuster moved from Germany to the Bay Area in 2015 for a job. Before that he was creative director at MoreSleep, the agency behind Freunde von Freunden.

The family found an Eichler house in Sunnyvale, in the middle of Silicon Valley, and filled it with design classics brought from home. Free time moved outdoors. BMX at the Santa Clara P.A.L. track, the skate park at Lake Cunningham in San Jose, surf at Capitola Beach.

Read the story on Freunde von Freunden ↗

So much more happens outdoors.

03 — Los Angeles

#### Advocacy through industry.

Raan, Shea and Stenn Parton grew up in Santa Barbara and now live in Los Angeles. Their label Apolis links small manufacturers around the world to a wider market. Jute market bags made in Bangladesh. Alpaca knits from Peru.

The story moves between their concept store Alchemy Works at Lido Marina in Newport Beach, a design market in West Hollywood and an evening surf near Santa Barbara.

Read the story on Freunde von Freunden ↗

L.A. really celebrates passion more than pedigree.

Three portraits for Visit California, published on Friends of Friends in summer 2016. Each story combined a written interview with a photo essay. The Ventura story added an eight-minute film.

The content was made with specific audiences in mind and shared with media partners internationally.

## Vitra. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/vitra-brand-strategy.html

Brand strategy, the FvF Apartment and the Homes & Workplaces series for Vitra, home of Eames, Prouvé and generations of design history.

Strategy

"Good design improves the quality of life."

Brand strategy, the FvF Apartment and the Homes & Workplaces series for Vitra, home of Eames, Prouvé and generations of design history.

Vitra is the Swiss furniture company behind the work of Eames, Prouvé and Girard. Working with a brand like this starts with what already works, then finds the contemporary form that reaches new audiences.

The brand strategy kept the design legacy and made its relevance clear for today. Editorial strategy and art direction connected the archive to contemporary design culture.

01 — FvF Apartment, Berlin

#### A real apartment, furnished as a statement.

With Vitra, Friends of Friends created the FvF Apartment in Berlin-Mitte: a 65sqm flat furnished entirely with Vitra and Artek pieces, designed as a space for the community rather than a showroom. It hosted shoots, press days and dinners, and became a blueprint for how the brand's furniture lives in everyday spaces.

02 — Vitra Workbays App

#### A 3D configurator for a new way of working.

For the launch of Vitra Workbays, the micro-architectural system by Ronan & Erwan Bouroullec, a free iPad app was conceived, designed and programmed. It lets users explore each Workbay from every angle, configure size, colour and interior elements in 3D, browse sample scenarios, and find nearby Vitra dealers.

03 — Homes & Workplaces · 2012–2018

#### Vitra in the homes and studios of the network.

Homes & Workplaces was a long-running editorial and film series with Vitra on Friends of Friends. The features visited people who live and work with Vitra furniture, among them Erik Spiekermann in Berlin, Alvaro Catalán de Ocón in Madrid and Clement Pascal in Bushwick, New York.

Short documentary films profiled workplaces and projects Vitra supports. Interior architect Sevil Peach in London talks about offices that left the cubicle behind for open, shared space. Artist Tobias Rehberger in Frankfurt walks through his studio and 24 Stops, the trail that leads to the Vitra Campus.

Sevil Peach Interior architect · London · 2017

Tobias Rehberger Artist · Frankfurt · 2018

Website redesign and art direction for Europe's leading insurtech: making insurance simple, transparent, and human through editorial photography and clean digital design.

Digital · Campaign

"Designing the digital future of insurance."

Website redesign and art direction for Europe's leading insurtech: making insurance simple, transparent, and human through editorial photography and clean digital design.

wefox makes finding and using insurance simpler and more transparent. They needed a website that better communicated this mission.

Our redesign reflects wefox's product: clean, straightforward and accessible. The uncluttered, dual-language website contains eye-catching diagrams and modelling that depict the simplicity of getting a wefox insurance quote through their phone app.

## Weiler. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/weiler-brand-identity.html

A new visual identity and website for Weiler, the reinvention of a family-run liquor distillery operating near the Bodensee since 1926.

Identity · Digital · Content

"Distilling a century of tradition into a new look."

A new visual identity and website for Weiler, the reinvention of a family-run liquor distillery operating near the Bodensee since 1926.

Weiler is the reinvention of a family-run liquor distillery, operating near the Bodensee since 1926. The studio crafted a new visual identity steeped in family history, and a website that communicates the magic of making apple schnapps the old-fashioned way.

The Weiler logo is inspired by old liquor bottles from small distilleries throughout Germany. To accompany the wordmark, the studio created a custom stamp based on the “W” of the family crest, used as a seal of authenticity.

A seal of authenticity, distilled by hand.

Each distillation produces around 300 bottles sold in limited batches to selected shops. The bottle's label is customisable, allowing it to adapt over the years; the distiller's name, year of production and bottle number are handwritten, and each batch is manually stamped with the family seal.

The studio created a crop of visual assets and content for the brand's social and online presence in collaboration with sister agency Friends of Friends, who featured an in-depth profile of Johannes Weber and the distillery's history.

Live site: weilerbrand.de ↗

Collaborators: Friends of Friends

Year: 2019

## Wildling – Regenerative Sounds. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/wildling-regenerative-sounds.html

Interactive digital experience for B Corp-certified footwear brand Wildling, using soundscapes from the Rhodope Mountains to highlight their collaboration with Rewilding Europe.

Digital · Campaign

"An antidote to retail therapy."

Interactive digital experience for B Corp-certified footwear brand Wildling, drawing on soundscapes recorded in the Rhodope Mountains to bring Rewilding Europe's conservation work to life.

Wildling is a B Corp-certified footwear company working to make a positive environmental impact. To highlight their collaboration with Rewilding Europe, they needed an experience that went beyond product.

Using sounds and visuals recorded in the Rhodope Mountains of Bulgaria, the experience gives visitors a moment of mindfulness. Three soundscapes, morning, afternoon, night, invite users to slow down and connect with something real.

01 — Concept

#### Purpose before product.

The experience was built around sounds recorded on site by audio artist Jonas Urbat. Organic shapes mirror the rhythm of the audio and act as clipping masks for contextual imagery.

02 — Interface

#### Design that gets out of the way.

Controls blend into the visualisation and can be hidden entirely. Backgrounds and interface colours shift with the time of day, adapting the mood without interrupting the experience.

Sound, shape, stillness.

An interactive experience for Wildling that turns nature recordings into a moment of mindfulness, prioritising purpose over product and the environment over the brand.

Collaboration with audio artist Jonas Urbat. Built for an international audience through Wildling's digital platform.

Live site: www.wildling.shoes/regenerative-sounds ↗

Collaborators: Jonas Urbat (audio)

Year: 2022

## Windsor. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/windsor-portrait-film-series.html

Portraits and films for German fashion brand Windsor, produced with Friends of Friends in Buenos Aires, Helsinki, Frankfurt and Byron Bay.

Editorial · Film

"Four cities, seen through the people who shape them."

Portraits and films for German fashion brand Windsor, produced with Friends of Friends in Buenos Aires, Helsinki, Frankfurt and Byron Bay.

Windsor is a German premium fashion brand for women and men.

From 2019 to 2020, Friends of Friends produced an ongoing portrait series for the brand. Each story visits a creative person where they live and work. The series started in Buenos Aires and moved on to Helsinki, Frankfurt and Byron Bay. Two of the stories became short films. In Frankfurt, a three-part series marked the opening of Windsor's first store in the city.

01 — Buenos Aires · 2019

#### A house for many disciplines.

Guadalupe García is the creative director of Casa Cavia in Palermo. The 1927 townhouse holds a restaurant, a coffee bar, a florist, a cocktail bar and a small publishing house. Each part has its own host.

She trained as a filmmaker. That eye now goes into light and plating. The story follows her through the house and out into the city.

##### Guadalupe García

02 — Helsinki · 2019

#### Room for surprise.

Tero Kuitunen works across product, spatial and concept design. He curates exhibitions and produces them too. Ceramics taught him to leave space for chance. Nothing is certain until the kiln opens.

Touch runs through his work. Objects are meant to be handled. The story became a short film, shot in his studio and in a snowy Helsinki.

##### Tero Kuitunen

Read the story on Friends of Friends ↗

I know something is good when I'm not one hundred percent sure what exactly it will be.

03 — Frankfurt · 2019

#### One city, three portraits.

Windsor opened its first Frankfurt store in August 2019, on Hochstraße near the Opernplatz. To mark the opening, FvF Productions made a three-part portrait series with Frankfurt creatives from different fields. It ran on Instagram in the autumn.

James and David Ardinast are brothers and restaurateurs. Since 2002 they have opened a string of places in the city, among them Chez Ima, later Bar Shuka, Maxie Eisen and Stanley Diamond. Their roots are Israeli and American. Their grandparents ran pubs in Höchst. A longer interview with the brothers ran on Friends of Friends.

Photographer Evelyn Dragan closed the series.

04 — Byron Bay · 2020

#### Work and life as one pursuit.

Saasha Burns and Sam Leetham run the wellness brand BEAR from their home in Byron Bay, on Australia's east coast. Vitamins and natural skincare. The couple first met in the town as school leavers.

The photo story and film move between their mid-century furnished home, a local café and the beach, where many of their ideas start.

##### Saasha Burns and Sam Leetham

Read the story on Friends of Friends ↗

Wellness is our greatest luxury.

Four stories over two years, each built around one person or pair and the place they work from.

Friends of Friends produced photography and interviews for every story, and film for two of them. The portraits ran on Friends of Friends. The Frankfurt series supported the store opening on Instagram.

Live site: windsor.de ↗

Collaborators: FvF Productions

Year: 2019–2020

## Wirtschaftsclub Düsseldorf. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/wirtschaftsclub-dusseldorf-web-design.html

Website redesign for Wirtschaftsclub Düsseldorf, reimagining the digital home of one of Germany's top business clubs for a new generation of members.

Identity · Digital

"Exclusivity and authenticity, online."

Website redesign for Wirtschaftsclub Düsseldorf, reimagining the digital home of one of Germany's top business clubs for a broader, younger audience.

WCD is the number one address for business and social connections in Düsseldorf, meeting rooms, dining, events, discussions. After a change of ownership, the brief was a comprehensive digital refresh.

The goal: reach a younger, more diverse audience while keeping existing members fully informed. A new design system built on the existing logo, with club-interior-inspired colour and new brand illustrations.

01 — Visual Identity

#### Built on what was already there.

The existing logo was reinterpreted for the web, a more modern design constructed around it. New brand elements, including illustrations, and a colour palette drawn directly from the club's interior.

02 — Website

#### Flexible enough to serve a growing club.

A set of modular content blocks handles all of the club's communication needs, memberships, room overviews, event listings, in a system designed to scale.

Where business and culture meet.

A comprehensive digital refresh for one of Germany's top business clubs, new visual identity, content system, and website built to attract a younger audience without losing the club's established character.

Part of an ongoing partnership with IAC, the club's owners.

Live site: www.wirtschaftsclubduesseldorf.de ↗

Year: 2022

## Ziegert. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/ziegert-real-estate-event.html

An art-focused real estate concept for Ziegert, filling six empty Kreuzberg lofts with sculptural installations designed to draw a crowd.

Campaign · Event · Digital

"A conceptual take on selling real estate."

An art-focused real estate concept for Ziegert, filling six empty Kreuzberg lofts with sculptural installations designed to draw a crowd.

To help Ziegert sell six unique, empty lofts in the centre of Kreuzberg, the studio devised an art-focused real estate concept featuring sculptural installations designed to draw a crowd.

To go new ways means to be courageous and to try things out. Inspired by the space, the studio thought about how it could be used temporarily for the marketing phase of the lofts — concluding that nothing is more natural than filling empty rooms with people.

There is nothing as liberating as starting with nothing.

Art was chosen as the ideal attraction: a reason to visit the empty lofts and fill them with life, ahead of the marketing phase for the six units.

Sculptural installations turned vacant rooms into a destination, drawing visitors into spaces they might otherwise never have entered.

Year: 2020

---

## Zumtobel. Frederik Frede

URL: https://frederikfrede.com/zumtobel-light-editorial-series.html

Light in art, design and architecture: a Friends of Friends editorial series for Austrian lighting maker Zumtobel, 2019 to 2021.

Editorial

How light shapes the way people live and work.

Light in art, design and architecture: a Friends of Friends editorial series for Austrian lighting maker Zumtobel, 2019 to 2021.

Zumtobel makes lighting in Dornbirn, Austria, for museums, offices and public buildings. Architects and lighting designers know the brand. A wider design audience mostly meets its work without noticing it.

The editorial series on Friends of Friends looked at how light inspires art, design and architecture. Portraits visited architects, curators and designers in Zurich, Vorarlberg and Vienna. Two essays covered light and health, and the future of the office. Zumtobel also contributed to the furnishing concept of the Friends Space in Berlin.

##### Formats and years

2019

Portraits

Architect Zhang Xi in Zurich, curator Verena Konrad in Vorarlberg

2019

Essays

Light and wellbeing; new approaches to the office

2021

Portrait

Designer Harald Gründl of EOOS in Vienna

01 — Zurich · 2019

#### Feng shui and a logo made of light.

Zhang Xi is founding partner and CEO of EXH Design, an architecture and interior studio with offices in Shanghai and Zurich. Her approach draws on feng shui: maximise the good energy, divert the bad.

For the Zurich office of the Chinese bank ICBC, the historic facade could not carry a sign. Zumtobel built an illuminated logo instead and hung it above the boardroom table, visible from the street.

##### Zhang Xi · EXH Design

Read on Friends of Friends ↗

02 — Vorarlberg · 2019

#### Craft, concrete and daylight.

Verena Konrad directs the Vorarlberger Architektur Institut in Dornbirn, Zumtobel’s home town. The region’s tight network of craftspeople and architects has produced a building culture known far beyond Austria.

The portrait follows her through the valley and into the buildings she uses to explain it: timber, rammed earth, exposed concrete and the light that falls on them.

##### Verena Konrad · vai

Read on Friends of Friends ↗

03 — Essays · 2019

#### Light as a nutrient.

Two essays widened the series beyond portraits. The first looked at research on light and wellbeing, including Zumtobel’s office lighting study with the Fraunhofer Institute and the tunable systems that came out of it. The second asked four experts, among them Zumtobel lighting application manager Daniel Leiter, what the office of the next decade will need.

Light and wellbeing ↗ · The future office ↗

04 — Vienna · 2021

#### Fifteen years of working together.

Harald Gründl co-founded the design studio EOOS in Vienna in 1995. EOOS and Zumtobel have worked together for close to fifteen years, most recently on the SUPERSYSTEM Integral collection and a new version of the VIVO spotlight system.

The portrait covers responsibility in design, working through a crisis, and why good products should last.

##### Harald Gründl · EOOS

Read on Friends of Friends ↗

Light is never the last decision.

An editorial series for Zumtobel, produced by Friends of Friends from 2019 to 2021. Portraits and essays on light in art, design and architecture.

Photographed in Zurich, Vorarlberg and Vienna and published on Friends of Friends.
